In the midrash Rabbi Abba says every הָרִים in Tanach is mountains but this one, which is exaltations, since a man is not exalted by these ways; and what does Hakadosh Baruch Hu do? He takes property from one and gives it to another.

גִּדַּלְתִּי וְרוֹמַמְתִּי (Yeshayahu 1:2), I reared and exalted, אֲרוֹמִמְךָ אֱלוֹהַי הַמֶּלֶךְ (Tehillim 145:1), I will exalt You, my Elokim the King, and רוֹמְמוֹת אֵל בִּגְרוֹנָם (Tehillim 149:6), the exaltations of Hashem in their throat. He says the whole sense is raising up. Rabbi Yonah divided between them, and there is no need, for separating one thing from another is itself a raising. So too וּכְסִילִים מֵרִים קָלוֹן: a fool raises shame and brings it upon himself.

more.h: The palace, and the precious stone
more.t: וְאַרְמוֹן עַל־מִשְׁפָּטוֹ יֵשֵׁב (Yirmiyahu 30:18), and a palace shall stand on its own place, may be from this sense, since it is a high building; he has already given it as a root of its own. רָאמוֹת וְגָבִישׁ (Iyov 28:18) is one of the precious stones, and some explain it like אַלְמוֹנִים, the thing called coral in the vernacular.

דרך.sense: To tread, and so to press the winepress and to draw the bow; דֶּרֶךְ, a way, and from it a man's custom, his dealings, and the mitzvos he walks in.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר דָּרַךְ־בָּהּ (Devarim 1:36), the land he trod on, דָּרַךְ כּוֹכָב מִיַּעֲקֹב (Bamidbar 24:17), a star has stepped forth from Yaakov, and אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרֹךְ כַּף־רַגְלְכֶם (Yehoshua 1:3), wherever the sole of your foot treads. Standing of itself, לֹא־הִדְרִיכֻוהוּ בְנֵי־שָׁחַץ (Iyov 28:8), the proud beasts have not trodden it. Taking an object, יַדְרֵךְ עֲנָוִים בַּמִּשְׁפָּט (Tehillim 25:9), He leads the humble in judgment, and הַדְרִיכֵנִי בַאֲמִתֶּךָ (Tehillim 25:5), lead me in Your truth. מְנוּחָה הִדְרִיכֻהוּ (Shoftim 20:43) he reads as from rest they drove him, and so Targum Yonasan, מִבֵּית נְיַחֲהוֹן טְרָדוּנוּן, from the house of their rest they drove them. With an added mem, מִדְרַךְ כַּף־רָגֶל (Devarim 2:5), the treading of the sole of a foot; and in this sense תִּדְרְכִי נַפְשִׁי עֹז (Shoftim 5:21), which lacks the beis of service and means you shall trample the enemies in strength.

דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ נֵלֵךְ (Bamidbar 20:17), we will go by the king's road, and זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ (Yeshayahu 30:21), this is the way, walk in it. לַעֲשׂוֹת דַּרְכּוֹ (Shoftim 17:8) is to make his way on from them and to stay there. פֶּן־יֶאֱנַף וְתֹאבְדוּ דֶרֶךְ (Tehillim 2:12) he reads as you will be lost from the side of the way, that is, your way is to be lost, as וְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים תֹּאבֵד (Tehillim 1:6); and in the same way נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30) is one whose leaves wither.

אָנֹכִי הֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (Melachim I 2:2) is as the custom is; כִּי־הִשְׁחִית כָּל־בָּשָׂר אֶת־דַּרְכּוֹ עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 6:12) is his manner; and כִּי־דֶרֶךְ נָשִׁים לִי (Bereishis 31:35) is the custom of women, which is niddah, as אֹרַח כַּנָּשִׁים (Bereishis 18:11). וּמַטֵּהוּ יִשָּׂא־עָלֶיךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְרָיִם (Yeshayahu 10:24) is after the manner of Mitzrayim, as the Egyptians used to strike you, and וּנְשָׂאוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְרָיִם (Yeshayahu 10:26) is after His own manner in Mitzrayim and the great hand He showed in them: He will lift it off you and finish it, or else He will raise His staff over him as He roused it over the sea.

more.h: Why all of them are one sense
more.t: He says they are one sense, since a man's desires, his dealings and whatever he exerts himself in are all called דֶּרֶךְ, and so are the mitzvos and the aveiros, as אֶת־הַדֶּרֶךְ יֵלְכוּ בָהּ (Shemos 18:20), the way they shall walk in, and דֶּרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים (Tehillim 1:6), the way of the righteous. On דַּרְכֵי עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 12:16), the ways of My people, he notes that the dalet is held by a ga'ya and that the Mesorah has no ga'ya there.

more.h: The winepress and the threshing floor
more.t: כְּדֹרֵךְ בְּגַת (Yeshayahu 63:2), as one treading in a winepress, אַתָּה תִדְרֹךְ־זַיִת וְלֹא־תָסוּךְ שֶׁמֶן (Michah 6:15), you shall tread olives and not anoint with oil, which Ben Asher reads with a cholam and Ben Naftali with a kamatz chatuf, and דֹּרְכִים גִּתּוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת (Nechemiah 13:15), treading winepresses on Shabbos. כְּגֹרֶן עֵת הִדְרִיכָהּ (Yirmiyahu 51:33) is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden, and their sense is treading and threshing. דָּרַכְתָּ בַיָּם סוּסֶיךָ (Chavakuk 3:15) he reads either as that they trod so in the mire of many waters, or as that You trod in the sea upon Your horses, which are the clouds.

דָּרַךְ קַשְׁתּוֹ (Eichah 2:4), he drew his bow, and וְכָל־קַשְּׁתֹתָיו דְּרֻכוֹת (Yeshayahu 5:28), all his bows drawn. Since drawing the bow draws the arrow with it, the word is used of the arrow too, דָּרְכוּ חִצָּם דָּבָר מָר (Tehillim 64:4), they have aimed their arrow, a bitter word. So וַיַּדְרְכוּ אֶת־לְשׁוֹנָם (Yirmiyahu 9:2), and they bend their tongue.

שׂרה.sense: One line. He gives שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים, you contended with Elokim, and the noun הַמִּשְׂרָה, the dominion, and says the sense is known.

more.t: וּבְאוֹנוֹ שָׂרָה אֶת־אֱלֹהִים (Hoshea 12:4), in his strength he contended with Elokim, and כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 32:29), for you have contended with Elokim; and the noun לְמַרְבֵּה הַמִּשְׂרָה (Yeshayahu 9:6), for the increase of the dominion. He adds only that the sense is known, and does not define it.

שׁרה.sense: מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים, a steeping of grapes; שִׁרְיָן, a coat of mail; and הַשָּׁרוֹן, which they explain as a land of plain and a fat place.

more.t: Rabbi Yehudah put שֵׁרִיתִיךָ לְטוֹב (Yirmiyahu 15:11), I have released you for good, under this root, and Rabbi Yonah wrote the same, both reading it like the Targum's וּמְשָׁרֵא קִטְרִין (Daniel 5:12), a looser of knots. He himself has written it under another root. His father reads תַּחַת־כָּל־הַשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׁרֵהוּ (Iyov 37:3) from this, that He looses the binding of the clouds and rains upon the corners of the earth; others read the same words from steeping. שָׁרוֹתַיִךְ מַעֲרָבֵךְ (Yechezkel 27:25) he has written under another root again.

וְכָל־מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים (Bamidbar 6:3), anything steeped from grapes, which he says is known from the words of Chazal: אין שורין דיו וסממנין, one may not steep ink and dyes, and ולא במי משרה, and not in water in which flax has been steeped.

וַיִּלְבַּשׁ צְדָקָה כַּשִּׁרְיָן (Yeshayahu 59:17), he put on righteousness as a coat of mail, בֵּין הַדְּבָקִים וּבֵין הַשִּׁרְיָן (Melachim I 22:34), between the joints and the mail, and וּמִשְׁקַל הַשִּׁרְיוֹן (Shmuel I 17:5), the weight of the mail. וְשִׁרְיוֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂים is one made in the manner of scales, and with a heh, חֲנִית מַסָּע וְשִׁרְיָה (Iyov 41:18). The plural is וְשִׁרְיֹנוֹת וּקְשָׁתוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 26:14), coats of mail and bows.

חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן (Shir HaShirim 2:1), the rose of the Sharon, and הָיָה הַשָּׁרוֹן כָּעֲרָבָה (Yeshayahu 33:9), the Sharon has become like a plain: they explained it as a land of level ground and a fat place, and so וְעַל־הַבָּקָר הָרֹעִים בַּשָּׁרוֹן (Divrei HaYamim I 27:29), the cattle grazing in the Sharon. שִׁרְטַי הַשָּׁרוֹנִי is a name.

ירה.sense: Three senses: to cast or shoot; to teach, and from it תּוֹרָה; and rain, the יוֹרֶה. He sets out how תּוֹרָה, מִשְׁפָּט, חֹק and מִשְׁמֶרֶת differ.

more.t: יָרָה בַיָּם (Shemos 15:4), He cast into the sea, הַמַּצֵּבָה אֲשֶׁר יָרִיתִי (Bereishis 31:51), the pillar I have set up, וְיָרִיתִי לָכֶם גּוֹרָל (Yehoshua 18:6), I will cast lots for you, and לִירוֹת בְּמוֹ־אֹפֶל (Tehillim 11:2), to shoot in the dark. With an alef in place of the heh, לִירוֹא בַּחִצִּים וּבָאֲבָנִים גְּדֹלוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 26:15), to shoot arrows and great stones. In the passive, אוֹ־יָרֹה יִיָּרֶה (Shemos 19:13), or he shall surely be shot. וַנִּירָם אָבַד חֶשְׁבּוֹן he reads as we shot at them and fought them until Cheshbon perished. הַמּוֹרִים אֶל־עֲבָדֶךָ (Shmuel II 11:24), the shooters at your servants, וַיִּמְצָאֻהוּ הַמּוֹרִים אֲנָשִׁים בַּקָּשֶׁת (Shmuel I 31:3), the archers found him, and וַיֹּרֵם אֱלֹהִים (Tehillim 64:8): all of these are casting. From this sense his father reads מִי כָמֹהוּ מוֹרֶה (Iyov 36:22) as one who casts down and brings low to the earth.

אֲשֶׁר הוֹרָהוּ יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן (Melachim II 12:3), which Yehoyada the kohen taught him, וַיֹּרֵנִי וַיֹּאמֶר לִי (Mishlei 4:4), he taught me and said to me, הוֹרוּנִי וַאֲנִי אַחֲרִישׁ (Iyov 6:24), teach me and I will be silent, וְלֹא־שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּקוֹל מוֹרָי (Mishlei 5:13), I did not listen to the voice of my teachers, and וּלְהוֹרֹת נָתַן בְּלִבּוֹ (Shemos 35:34), He put it in his heart to teach. מִגִּבְעַת הַמּוֹרֶה בָּעֵמֶק (Shoftim 7:1) may be from this, or else a place name; if from this, a watchman stood on the hill who would give word to those in the valley when an army came upon them, and so Targum Yonasan, מִגִבְעֲתָא דְמִסְתַּכְיָא, from the hill of the lookout. Rabbi Yehudah said הֹרוֹ וְהֹגוֹ מִלֵּב דִּבְרֵי־שָׁקֶר (Yeshayahu 59:13) may be from this root too, but he has written it under another root, and that is the correct one.

more.h: תּוֹרָה, and the words beside it
more.t: The noun from teaching is תּוֹרָה, אֶת־הַחֻקִּים וְאֶת־הַתּוֹרֹת (Shemos 18:20), the statutes and the teachings, and מִצְוֹתַי חֻקּוֹתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי (Bereishis 26:5), My mitzvos, My statutes and My teachings; and possibly וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָדָם (Shmuel II 7:19), and this is the teaching of man. He separates four: הַתּוֹרָה is the manner of the mitzvah, how it is to be done; הַמִּשְׁפָּט is a man's judgment between himself and his fellow; הַחֹק is the thing decreed upon a man to do, whether as a mitzvah or as a custom; and הַמִּשְׁמֶרֶת is the guarding against transgressing a mitzvah and the fence made about it. Each is a sense of its own, but in places one comes for another.

יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ (Devarim 11:14) is the early and the late rain, and with an alef for the heh, וּמַרְוֶה גַם־הוּא יוֹרֶא (Mishlei 11:25): one who gives the poor drink is himself called a יוֹרֶה, like the rain that waters the earth. So too אֶת־הַמּוֹרֶה לִצְדָקָה (Yoel 2:23), the rain for righteousness, and וְהָיוּ עֵינֶיךָ רֹאוֹת אֶת־מוֹרֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 30:20), your eyes shall see your rain. וְלֹא־יִכָּנֵף עוֹד מוֹרֶיךָ is that your rain shall no longer be gathered in, for they were in a time of drought, as it says לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ, the bread of affliction and the water of oppression; he was announcing plenty to them, that the rain would not be held back and they would see with their own eyes that it was near. Others read מוֹרֶיךָ from the second sense, your teachers who show you the straight way, who shall not be far off at the corner of the earth, and they are Chizkiyahu and his officers. His father reads אֱלֹהָיו יוֹרֶנּוּ (Yeshayahu 28:26) from the third sense, that He will give him rain.

לבן.sense: White; לְבֵנָה, a brick, perhaps so named because what is burnt whitens; הַלְּבָנָה, the moon; לִבְנֶה, a tree; and לְבוֹנָה, the resin of a tree.

more.h: The brick, and the brick kiln
more.t: וַתְּהִי לָהֶם הַלְּבֵנָה לְאָבֶן (Bereishis 11:3), the brick served them for stone, with the verb נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים (Bereishis 11:3), let us make bricks, and לִלְבֹּן הַלְּבֵנִים (Shemos 5:7), to make the bricks. The kiln in which they are fired is called מַלְבֵּן, as בַּמַּלְבֵּן (Shmuel II 12:31), which he reads as that he burnt them in the brick kiln. Yonasan renders that word וּגְרַר יַתְהוֹן בְּשׁוּקַיָא, he dragged them through the streets, putting them to a hard and contemptible death; and why streets? Perhaps he holds a street is called מַלְבֵּן because it is set with colonnades ordered on this side and that, as Chazal have מלבנות התבואה, beds of grain, so called because they are ordered, and מלבנות הפתחים, the doorposts on either side. בַּמֶּלֶט בַּמַּלְבֵּן (Yirmiyahu 43:9) is the place where bricks are made, and הַחֲזִיקִי מַלְבֵּן (Nachum 3:14) is build up the brick kiln.

more.h: Whether the brick comes from white
more.t: He says the bricks may be from the sense of whiteness, since everything burnt in fire whitens, and so יִתְבָּרְרוּ וְיִתְלַבְּנוּ וְיִצָּרְפוּ (Daniel 12:10), they shall be purified and made white and refined; and so Chazal said מלבנן באור והן טהורים, one whitens them in fire and they are tahor.

כְּזֶרַע גַּד לָבָן (Shemos 16:31): the mon was white and its grains were like coriander seed. מַחְשׂף הַלָּבָן (Bereishis 30:37), the white laid bare, וּלְבֶן־שִׁנַּיִם מֵחָלָב (Bereishis 49:12), white of teeth from milk, and כֵּהוֹת לְבָנֹת (Vayikra 13:39), dull white spots. Standing of itself, כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ (Yeshayahu 1:18), they shall be white as snow, and הִלְבִּינוּ שָׂרִיגֶיהָ (Yoel 1:7), her branches have whitened, that is, they dried and turned white. Taking an object, וּלְבָרֵר וְלַלְבֵּן עַד־עֵת קֵץ (Daniel 11:35), to purify and to whiten until the time of the end, where the form should have been וּלְהַלְבֵּן, to whiten, and with the heh gone its vowel was thrown onto the lamed.

Rabbi Yonah takes לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר (Shemos 24:10) as a noun, a white sapphire, and so said the Gaon, that the sapphire is white. Ibn Ezra wrote that the sapphire is red, his proof being אָדְמוּ עֶצֶם מִפְּנִינִים סַפִּיר גִּזְרָתָם (Eichah 4:7), they were ruddier of bone than pearls, their form a sapphire, where the statement is doubled as in זַכּוּ נְזִירֶיהָ מִשֶּׁלֶג צַחוּ מֵחָלָב, her nezirim were purer than snow, whiter than milk; and further, why does the pasuk say כמעשה, like the work of, and not כמראה, like the appearance of? He holds rather that it is from לְבָנָה, the moon, as חֶשְׁכַת־מַיִם (Tehillim 18:12) is from חֲשֵׁכָה, darkness, and that לבנת הספיר is like the sapphire stone Yechezkel saw. The derash takes it that they saw the likeness of a brick under the feet of the Kisei HaKavod, to see and remember that Yisrael were enslaved under the hand of Mitzrayim at the work of bricks.

more.h: The moon, the tree, and לְבוֹנָה
more.t: וְחָפְרָה הַלְּבָנָה (Yeshayahu 24:23) is the moon, called so because it appears white. תַּחַת אַלּוֹן וְלִבְנֶה (Hoshea 4:13), under oak and poplar, and מַקַּל לִבְנֶה (Bereishis 30:37), a rod of poplar, are a tree named from being white, which Rabbi Yonah wrote is the one called so in Arabic. לְבֹנָה זַכָּה (Vayikra 24:7), pure levonah, is known, and עִם כָּל־עֲצֵי לְבוֹנָה (Shir HaShirim 4:14) are the trees the levonah comes from, for levonah is the resin of a tree.

Some take לבן as the name of one of David's enemies, at whose death David made the mizmor; some take it as an inversion of נָבָל. His father wrote that the lamed is a service letter and that it is the name of a singer, named in Divrei HaYamim among the second rank, זְכַרְיָהוּ בֵּן וְיַעֲזִיאֵל וּשְׁמִירָמוֹת (Divrei HaYamim I 15:18); David said the mizmor on the death of Golyas and the victory over the Pelishtim, and that singer played it. If you ask why it is not לְבֵן with a sheva, as לְאָסָף, since the article does not come on a man's name or a city's, the answer is that though it is not the way of the language it comes at times for the sake of definiteness, as אֲשֶׁר בַּשֶּׂכוּ (Shmuel I 19:22) and וַיִּפְקְדֵם בַּטְּלָאִים (Shmuel I 15:4); and here the article was used so the name should not be confused with the ordinary word for a son.

ספן.sense: To roof a house over and cover it in; close to it, to lie hidden. The סְפִינָה, a ship, is filed here too.

more.t: וַיִּסְפֹּן אֶת־הַבַּיִת (מלכים א' ו, ט), he roofed the house; וְסָפוּן בָּאֶרֶז (ירמיה כב, יד), panelled with cedar; לָשֶׁבֶת בְּבָֽתֵּיכֶם סְפוּנִים (חגי א, ד), to sit in your roofed houses. The noun is עַד־קִירוֹת הַסִּפֻּן (מלכים א' ו, טו), up to the walls of the ceiling. All of them are the roofing of houses and the covering of them.

חֶלְקַת מְחֹקֵק סָפוּן (דברים לג, כא) is a portion of a lawgiver, roofed over: the share of Bnei Gad was the portion of a lawgiver and a ruler, the whole of it built and roofed as it should be, a hint at the cities they took across the Yarden.
וּשְׂפֻנֵי טְמוּנֵי חֽוֹל (דברים לג, יט), the hidden things stored away in the sand, he puts near this sense, and notes that it is written with a sin, שפוני, hidden, standing like טמוני, buried.
אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי הַסְּפִינָה (יונה א, ה), to the innermost part of the ship, of which he says only that it is known.

חרס.sense: The sun; and in another sense the dry itch, named for the potsherd a man scratches himself with.

more.t: הָֽאֹמֵר לַחֶרֶס וְלֹא יִזְרָח (איוב ט, ז), who tells the sun not to rise, and בְּטֶרֶם יָבֹא הַחַרְסָה (שופטים יד, יח), before the sun went in. From this the eastern gate of the Beis HaMikdash is called שַׁעַר הַֽחַרְסִות (ירמיה יט, ב), because it stood square against the rising of the sun.
מִֽלְמַֽעֲלֵה הֶחָֽרֶס (שופטים ח, יג) Yonasan takes from this same sense, rendering it עַד לָא מֵעַל שִׁמְשָׁא, before the sun set.

A second sense, at וּבַגָּרָב וּבֶחָרֶס (דברים כח, כז), with the scab and with the cheres. It is the dry itch, and it carries this name because a man rubs it with a potsherd, as וַיִּֽקַּֽח־לוֹ חֶרֶשׂ לְהִתְגָּרֵד בּוֹ (איוב ב, ח), he took himself a potsherd to scrape himself with.

חזר.sense: One line: the pig, of which he says only that it is known; in the Mishnah the root is used a great deal for returning.

more.t: וְאֶֽת־ הַֽחֲזִיר (ויקרא יא, ז), and the pig, which he marks ידוע, known, and nothing further. He adds that in the Mishnah they used this root much in the language of חזרה, going back.

כתב.sense: To write; and the nouns, כְּתָב, a writing or a script, and מִכְתָּב, the thing written, whether graven or a letter sent.

more.t: וְכָתַב לָהּ סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת (דברים כד, א), he writes her a bill of severance; וְהִיא כְתוּבָה פָּנִים וְאָחוֹר (יחזקאל ב, י), written on the face of it and the back; כָּל־ הַכָּתוּב לַחַיִּים (ישעיה ד, ג), everyone written down for life; וְכָתוֹב בַּסֵּפֶר וְחָתוֹם (ירמיה לב, מד), written in the deed and sealed. וְזֶה יִכְתֹּב יָדוֹ (ישעיה מד, ה), and this one will write his hand to Hashem, he reads as writing with his hand.

On וַיִּכְתֹּב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרַת אֱלֹהִים (יהושע כד, כו), Yonasan renders that he wrote them וְאַצְנְעִינוּן בְּסֵפֶר אוֹרַיְתָא, and laid them up in the Sefer Torah. Chazal are divided (Makkos 11a): some say it is the eight pesukim from the death of Moshe to the end of the Torah, which Yehoshua wrote into the Torah; others say it is the parsha of the cities of refuge, which he wrote in his own sefer as they stand in the Torah. By the plain sense of the pasuk, he holds, it is the covenant Yehoshua cut with Yisrael that he wrote, and then Yonasan's rendering is the right one, since the words of that covenant cannot have been written into the Sefer Torah.

more.h: The noun for the writing itself
more.t: הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב (דברי הימים א' כח, יט), the whole of it in writing; מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה כִּכְתָבָהּ (אסתר ג, יב), every province in its own script. With a mem added, וְהַמִּכְתָּב מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים הוּא (שמות לב, טז), and the writing was the writing of Hashem.

כְתָב אֲשֶׁר־נִכְתָּב בְּשֵׁם־הַמֶּלֶךְ (אסתר ח, ח), a writ written in the king's name; and with a mem, וַיָּבֹא אֵלָיו מִכְתָּב מֵאֵֽלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא (דברי הימים ב' כא, יב), a letter came to him from Eliyahu HaNavi. In the passive, בְּשֵׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרשׁ נִכְתָּב (אסתר ג, יב), it was written in the name of Achashverosh.
וְעַל־לִבָּם אֶכְתֲּבֶנָּה (ירמיה לא, לג), I will write it on their heart: Ben Naftali points the tav with a sheva and a patach, Ben Asher with a kamatz chatuf.

וּכְתֹבֶת קַֽעֲקַע (ויקרא יט, כח), a tattoo mark: a man gouges into his flesh and writes in the incision. Where the middle letter is doubled, וּֽמְכַתְּבִים עָמָל כִּתֵּֽבוּ (ישעיה י, א), those who write out oppression, and he allows that the verb there may govern a third object.

לחם.sense: To eat, and לֶחֶם, food of every sort, bread most of all; from the same, מִלְחָמָה, war, where the sword eats on this side and that.

more.h: Eating, and food of every kind
more.t: כִּי לָֽחֲמוּ לֶחֶם רֶשַׁע (משלי ד, יז), for they have eaten the food of wickedness; כִּֽי־תֵשֵׁב לִלְחוֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁל (משלי כג, א), when you sit to eat with a ruler; לְכוּ לַֽחֲמוּ בְֽלַֽחֲמִי (משלי ט, ה), come, eat of my food. וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף (דברים לב, כד) he glosses אכולי רשף, eaten up by the fiery bolt, and some read וְשֹׁרֶשׁ רְתָמִים לַחְמָֽם (איוב ל, ד), the root of the broom is their food, from the same. Every לֶחֶם, he says, is a word for food in general: it falls on meat alone, אֶת־קָרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי (במדבר כח, ב), My offering, My food, for My fires, and לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה (ויקרא ג, יא); it takes in meat and terumos together at לֶחֶם אֱלֹהָיו (ויקרא כא, כב), and so מִלֶּחֶם אָבִיהָ תֹּאכֵל (ויקרא כב, יג), she eats of her father's food. It settled on bread more than on the rest because bread is the mainstay of what a man eats.

לְהוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ (תהלים קד, יד), to bring bread out of the earth, names the end the grass is for, since bread does not come out of the ground but through causes that go before it. So too צֶמַח בְּלִי יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ קֶּמַח (הושע ח, ז), growth that makes no flour: the end of the growth is the flour, though acts pass into acts before it is reached, and the flour is not the last end either, for the last end is the bread, in what suits a man.

נַשְׁחִיתָה עֵץ בְּלַחְמוֹ (ירמיה יא, יט) he takes as בפריו, with its fruit. His father reads the words turned about, נשחיתה לחמו בעץ, let us ruin his food with the tree, the tree called in Arabic דפל"א, which is a deadly poison; and of it, he says, was said that Hashem showed him a tree and he cast it into the water (שמות טו, כה), a miracle inside a miracle, as Chazal say. Yonasan renders in the same line, נִרְמֵי סַמָא דְמוֹתָא בְּמֵיכְלֵיהּ, let us cast deadly poison into his food.

מֵֽאָשֵׁר שְׁמֵנָה לַחְמוֹ (בראשית מט, כ) takes in every food: whatever his land brings out will be rich. שְׁמֵנָה, rich, belongs to his land, as though the pasuk said a rich land will be his bread, the words being cut short as at וּמַֽאֲכָלוֹ בְּרִאָֽה (חבקוק א, טז), his food is fat. Or else שְׁמֵנָה belongs to לַחְמוֹ and the loaf meant is an עוּגָה or a חַלָּה, which is feminine, as לֶחֶם תְּנוּפָה שְׁתַּיִם (ויקרא כג, יז), two loaves of waving, means חַלּוֹת, cakes.

more.h: War, and whom a man fights for
more.t: מִלְחָמָה, war, is of this same sense, because in war there is the eating of the sword from this side and from that. The verb: לְחַם אֶת־ לֹֽחֲמָֽי (תהלים לה, א), fight those who fight me, and לֹחֵם יִלְחָצֵֽנִי (תהלים נו, ב), a fighter presses me. In the passive form, אִם־ נִלְחֹם נִלְחַם בָּֽם (שופטים יא, כה), did he ever fight against them, and וַיִּלָּחֶם עִם־לִבְנָֽה (יהושע י, כט), he fought with Livnah. Where it takes עַל or a lamed it is fighting for someone: אֲֽשֶׁר־ נִלְחַם אָבִי עֲלֵיכֶם (שופטים ט, יז) is for your sake, and יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם (שמות יד, יד) is for you; but וַיִּלָּֽחֲמוּנִי חִנָּֽם (תהלים קט, ג) is they fought against me for nothing.

אָז לָחֶם שְׁעָרִים (שופטים ה, ח): Rabbi Yonah writes that לָחֶם is a past verb of the light form, on the measure of יָבֵשׁ חָצִיר (ישעיה מ, ז), the grass is withered, the segol standing here in place of a tzere; were it the heavy form the lamed would carry a patach as it usually does, and here it carries a kamatz. It may also be a noun on the pattern of חָמֵץ, leaven, so that the words say there was war in the gates, though this one has a segol and that one a tzere.

ככר.sense: A loaf of bread, and a piece of one; the plain of the Yarden; and the talent, a weight of gold or silver.

more.t: וְכִכַּר לֶחֶם אַחַת (שמות כט, כג), one loaf of bread, he reads as a large loaf, since the others named there were חלות and רקיקים, cakes and wafers.
וְכִכַּר ־לָחֶם (שמואל א' ב, לו) he takes as the Targum does, פִּתָּא דְלַחְמָא, that is to say a piece of bread.
כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן (בראשית יג, יא), whose Targum is מֵישַׁר יַרְדְּנָא, the level plain of the Yarden.

כִּכַּר זָהָב (שמות כה, לט), a talent of gold; וַיָּצַר כִּכְּרַיִם כֶּסֶף (מלכים ב' ה, כג), he bound up two talents of silver; וַיִּקַּח בְּיָדוֹ עֶשֶׂר כִּכְּרֵי ־כֶסֶף (מלכים ב' ה, ה), he took ten talents of silver in his hand. The common talent was sixty litrin, and the sanctuary's was double it, a hundred and twenty.

פתת.sense: To break into pieces; פַת, a piece of bread, and פִּתִּים, crumbs or morsels.

more.t: פָּתוֹת אֹתָהּ פִּתִּים (ויקרא ב, ו), break it into pieces, is a sense of cutting and breaking, and so פַת ־לֶחֶם (בראשית יח, ה), a piece of bread, וְאֹכַל פִּתִּי לְבַדִּי (איוב לא, יז), that I ate my morsel alone, and מִפִּתּוֹ תֹאכַל (שמואל ב' יב, ג), it would eat of his morsel.

מַשְׁלִיךְ קַֽרְחוֹ כְפִתִּים (תהלים קמז, יז), casting His ice like morsels, is like a thing broken up into bits; the word in its fuller form is וּבִפְתוֹתֵי לֶחֶם (יחזקאל יג, יט), for scraps of bread.

Rabbi Yehudah sets a further sense in this root, from וַֽהֲפִתִּיתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ (משלי כד, כח), which he reads as breaking your fellow with your lips, though by rule the word would be הֲפִתּוֹתָ with a cholam. He himself will treat it again under the root פָּתָה, to entice; and the breaking of this root can stand in it, he says, from the sense of the pasuk itself, אַל־תְּהִי עֵֽד־חִנָּם בְּרֵעֶךָ (משלי כד, כח), be no witness against your fellow without cause: witness against him for nothing and you break him and strike him with your lips.

חרר.sense: To be scorched and burnt up with heat; the חֲרָרָה, the cake baked on the coals, is named from it.

more.t: וְעַצְמִי־ חָרָה מִנִּי־חֹֽרֶב (איוב ל, ל), my bone is burnt with heat; וְחָרָה נְחֻשְׁתָּהּ (יחזקאל כד, יא), that its copper may glow; עַל־כֵּן חָרוּ ישְׁבֵי אֶרֶץ (ישעיה כד, ו), therefore the dwellers of the earth are scorched. In the passive, וְהָֽעֲצָמוֹת יֵחָֽרוּ (יחזקאל כד, י), the bones will be burnt; and with a chirik under the nun, נִחַר גְּרוֹנִי (תהלים סט, ד), my throat is parched, and וְעַצְמוֹתַי כְּמוֹקֵד נִחָֽרוּ (תהלים קב, ד), my bones are burnt as a hearth.

נָחַר מַפֻּחַ (ירמיה ו, כט), the bellows is scorched: the instrument they blow the fire with is kindled and burnt from standing so long in the fire, and the lead is spent, the lead the smiths put in with the silver in refining it so that the fire should not destroy the silver; and for all that, the wicked are not drawn off. It is a mashal for Yisrael. The navi speaks to them הַשְׁכֵּם וְהַֽעֲרֵב, early and late, until he is as one burnt up from speaking to them, his throat scorched from calling to them without stopping, as it says elsewhere עַל־כֵּן חָצַבְתִּי בַּנְּבִיאִים הֲרַגְתִּים בְּאִמְרֵי־פִי (הושע ו, ה), therefore I hewed at them by the nevi'im, I slew them with the words of My mouth; and with all this they take no rebuke and do not believe the navi's voice.

The noun is וְשָׁכַן חֲרֵרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר (ירמיה יז, ו), he dwells in the parched places of the wilderness, a sense of burning and kindling from much heat; the single of חררים is חָרֵר or חֲרָרָה. From this the cake baked on the coals is called חֲרָרָה, as in ולא חררה על גבי גחלים (Shabbos 1:10), nor a cake upon coals, and it is called so because its face is scorched. Talmud Yerushalmi explains סַלֵּי חֹרִי (בראשית מ, טז) in the same way, that the baskets were full of חררות, such cakes.

more.h: Kindling a quarrel, and a fever
more.t: Where the first root letter is doubled, לְחַרְחַר ־רִֽיב (משלי כו, כא), to kindle a quarrel and set it alight; the patach under the second ches stands in place of a tzere. From the same, וּבַֽחַרְחֻר וּבַחֶרֶב (דברים כח, כב), with fever and with the sword, a sickness that burns from much heat.

עוף.sense: To fly; a second sense of darkness, which most read the other way as brightness; and a third, pointed differently, to grow weary, and so to thirst.

more.t: כַּֽחֲלוֹם יָעוּף (Iyov 20:8), he flies off like a dream; מֵחֵץ יָעוּף יוֹמָֽם (Tehillim 91:5), the arrow that flies by day; וַיָּעָף אֵלַי אֶחָד מִן־הַשְּׂרָפִים (Yeshayahu 6:6), one of the Serafim flew to me, where the first root letter is read with a short kamatz. Also כִּי־גָז חִישׁ וַנָּעֻֽפָה (Tehillim 90:10), it passes quickly and we fly away. Doubled, וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 1:20), and let birds fly over the earth; and turned back on itself, כָּעוֹף יִתְעוֹפֵף כְּבוֹדָם (Hoshea 9:11), their glory will fly off like a bird.

מֻעָף בִּיעָף (Daniel 9:21), made to fly swiftly, may belong to this root, its yud added as the yud of יְקוּם is added to קוּם, and he has set it out already under the root יָעַף. Rabbi Yehudah brings here מְגִלָּה עָפָֽה (Zecharyah 5:1), a flying scroll, and so the Targum, which renders it מְגִלָה פִּרְחָא, a flying scroll. Others read it as folded, from the Targum of וְכָפַלְתָּ (Shemos 26:9), which is וְתֵיעוּף.

תָּעֻפָה כַּבֹּקֶר תִּהְיֶֽה (Iyov 11:17), which he reads as: if you are in darkness now, you will be like the morning. So too עֹשֵׂה שַׁחַר עֵיפָה (Amos 4:13), He makes the dawn out of darkness, and אֶרֶץ עֵיפָתָה כְּמֽוֹ־אֹפֶל (Iyov 10:22), a land of gloom like darkness, that last carrying two feminine endings as יְשׁוּעָתָה does. His father writes that the land like darkness is the place the sun does not shine on for six months, lying off the line of the earth, out of reach of its light and far off; and that ולא סדרים, and no order, means there is no order of moon and stars there. The noun is מְעוּף צוּקָה (Yeshayahu 8:22), the gloom of distress, and in the passive כִּי לֹא מוּעָף לַֽאֲשֶׁר מוּצָק לָהּ (Yeshayahu 8:23): it was not made dark for Eretz Yisrael at the first as it is now, for the first trouble, when Pul king of Ashur exiled them, was light and took only Zevulun and Naftali away, while at the last Sancheriv bore down hard. מוּעָף may be a noun, and so מוּצָק. Rabbi Yehudah brings הֲתָעִיף עיניך בו (Mishlei 23:5) into this group as well.

more.h: Read the other way, as light
more.t: Most of the commentators take תָּעֻפָה כַּבֹּקֶר תִּהְיֶֽה and הֲתָעִיף עיניך בו in the opposite sense, of flashing and light, and explain עֹשֵׂה שַׁחַר עֵיפָה the same way. בְּעֽוֹפְפִי חַרְבִּי עַל־פְּנֵיהֶם (Yechezkel 32:10) is then when I make my sword flash and flame as I draw it from its sheath; or it belongs to the first sense, of movement, when I wave it and brandish it over them to kill, and movement, he says, lies near to flight. The noun here is doubled: בְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר (Iyov 3:9), the glow of dawn and its light. From the same the eye is called עפעף: לְֽעַפְעַפַּי תְּנוּמָֽה (Tehillim 132:4), slumber to my eyelids; עַפְעַפָּיו יִבְֽחֲנוּ בְּנֵי אָדָֽם (Tehillim 11:4), His eyes try the sons of man; וְעַל עַפְעַפַּי צַלְמָֽוֶת (Iyov 16:16); and וְעַפְעַפֵּינוּ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם (Yirmiyahu 9:17), our eyes will run with water, which Targum Yonasan renders וְגַלְגַלֵי עֵינָנָא יִגְרוּן מַיָא, the balls of our eyes will run with water.

From Chazal he brings אין מדליקין בצרי (Shabbos 25b), balsam is not lit, מפני שהוא עף, because it flies, that is, it darts and moves off the lamp and spatters here and there; and היתה מעופפת בזמן שכנפיה נוגעות בקן חייב לשלח, where the mother bird is only stirring, not flying but near to flight, and one is bound to send her away. So too, in his own view, וְעָפוּ בְכָתֵף פְּלִשְׁתִּים יָמָּה (Yeshayahu 11:14): Israel will move toward the flank of the Pelishtim to spoil and to plunder. בכתף stands as a construct although it is not pointed as one; Ben Asher wrote that it came so because of the peh of פלשתים, to settle the reading.

עָֽיְפָה נַפְשִׁי לְהֹֽרְגִֽים (Yirmiyahu 4:31), my soul is faint before the killers; וְהֽוּא־נִרְדַּם וַיָּעַף וַיָּמֹֽת (Shoftim 4:21), he was asleep and spent and died; and וַיָּעַף דָּוִֽד (Shmuel II 21:15). These last two take a patach in the first root letter to keep them apart from וַיָּעָף אלי, which is the other sense. The adjective is עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ (Devarim 25:18), weary and worn. Since a weary man thirsts for water, a thirsty man is called עָיֵף by borrowing, though there is no weariness in him at all but thirst alone, as וְכַֽאֲשֶׁר יַֽחֲלֹם הַצָּמֵא (Yeshayahu 29:8), and as a thirsty man dreams he is drinking and wakes spent. So too ground that thirsts for rain: בְּאֶֽרֶץ־צִיָּה וְעָיֵף בְּלִי־מָֽיִם (Tehillim 63:2), in a dry and thirsty land without water; נַפְשִׁי כְּאֶֽרֶץ־ עֲיֵפָה לְךָ סֶֽלָה (Tehillim 143:6); and כְּצֵל סֶֽלַע־כָּבֵד בְּאֶרֶץ עֲיֵפָֽה (Yeshayahu 32:2). Some take וְעָפוּ בְכָתֵף פְּלִשְׁתִּים from this sense, and he has explained it under the root כָּתֵף.

חשׁב.sense: To think and to plan; to reckon a thing as something, or as nothing at all; to count and calculate; and the חֹשֵׁב, the weaver, whose craft goes by design.

more.t: וְשָׁאוּל חָשַׁב לְהַפִּיל אֶת־דָּוִד, Shaul planned to bring David down; וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה (Bereishis 50:20), you thought evil against me, which he continues with Hashem having thought it for good; and וְלֹֽא־יָדַעְתִּי כִּֽי־עָלַי חָֽשְׁבוּ מַֽחֲשָׁבוֹת (Yirmiyahu 11:19), I did not know they had laid plans against me. Where the verb is doubled, חִשַּׁבְתִּי יָמִים מִקֶּדֶם (Tehillim 77:6), I thought over days of old; וַֽאֲחַשְּׁבָה לָדַעַת זֹאת (Tehillim 73:16); מַה־ תְּחַשְּׁבוּן (Nachum 1:9), what do you plot against Hashem; לֵב אָדָם יְחַשֵּׁב דַּרְכּוֹ (Mishlei 16:9), a man's heart plans his way; and וְאֵלַי יְחַשְּׁבוּ (Hoshea 7:15). The sense of thought, he says, is known.

וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ עֵלִי לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה (Shmuel I 1:13), Eli took her for a drunken woman; and יַחְשֹׁב תְּהוֹם לְשֵׂיבָֽה (Iyov 41:24), which he explains as one who sees the deep white and takes it for a head of grey hair. In וְהָאֳנִיָּה חִשְּׁבָה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר (Yonah 1:4) it is the men of the ship who thought she would break, the way וְכָל־ הָאָרֶץ בָּאוּ מִצְרַיְמָה (Bereishis 41:57) means all the men of the land, and וַתִּרְעַב כָּל־אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 41:55) the like.

Since a craft goes by thought, the word is used of craftsmanship: לַחְשֹׁב מַֽחֲשָׁבֹת (Shemos 31:4), to devise designs, and מַֽעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב תַּֽעֲשֶׂה אֹתָֽם (Shemos 26:1), of designer's work. The noun is וְחֵשֶׁב אפדתו (Shemos 28:8), the band of its efod, with five vowel points. On מעשה רוקם כמעשה חושב the Chachamim in Yoma 72b ask what it means, and Rabbi Elazar answers שרוקמין במקום שחושבים, that they embroider where they weave; a braisa there teaches רוקם מעשה מחט ולפיכך פרצוף אחד, embroidery is needlework and so has one face, חושב מעשה אורג, לפיכך שני פרצופין, the designer's work is weaving and so has two faces.

The same word serves for reckoning and for the philosopher's inquiry: וּבַקֵּשׁ חָכְמָה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן (Koheles 7:25), to seek wisdom and reckoning; כִּי אֵין מַֽעֲשֶׂה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן (Koheles 9:10); and וְהֵמָּה בִקְשׁוּ חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת רַבִּֽים (Koheles 7:29), with the shin doubled for ornament, which he takes as the devices and questions men raise over the Creator's work, why He made this so and why that was so, when He made man upright and all His work is in faithfulness. So וַיַּעַשׂ בִּירֽוּשָׁלַם חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 26:15). Of number: Hashem does not reckon iniquity to a man (Tehillim 32:2). In the passive, אַךְ לֹֽא־ יֵֽחָשֵׁב אִתָּם הַכֶּסֶף הַנִּתָּן עַל־יָדָם (Melachim II 22:7), no reckoning was made with them of the money given into their hand; where the verb is doubled, וְחִשַּׁב אֶת־שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ (Vayikra 25:27), he shall count the years of his sale, and וְלֹא יְחַשְּׁבוּ אֶת־הָֽאֲנָשִׁים (Melachim II 12:16); and turned back on itself, וּבַגּוֹיִם לֹא יִתְחַשָּֽׁב (Bamidbar 23:9).

more.h: Counted for nothing, or for much
more.t: Near to this is לֹא חָשַׁב אֱנֽוֹשׁ (Yeshayahu 33:8), which he glosses as he took no notice of them and counted them for nothing; and so נִבְזֶה וְלֹא חֲשַׁבְנֻֽהוּ (Yeshayahu 53:3), despised, and we did not account him; אֲשֶׁר־כֶּסֶף לֹא יַחְשֹׁבוּ (Yeshayahu 13:17), who set no store by silver; and וּלְחֹֽשְׁבֵי שְׁמֽוֹ (Malachi 3:16), those who give heed to His name. יַֽחֲשָׁב לִי (Tehillim 40:18), Hashem will take account of me, means that his prayers and pleadings are reckoned before Him and that He takes notice of the poverty and want he is in; and from this the Chachamim in Avodah Zarah 25b call an honoured man אדם חשוב, a man of account. In the passive, אֵין כֶּסֶף לֹא נֶחְשָׁב בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה לִמְאֽוּמָה (Melachim I 10:21), which he explains as there being no silver among the vessels at all, since they were all gold, because silver counted for nothing in Shlomo's days; and so וְנֶחְשַׁב לָכֶם תְּרֽוּמַתְכֶם (Bamidbar 18:27), מַדּוּעַ נֶחְשַׁבְנוּ כַבְּהֵמָה (Iyov 18:3), כִּֽי־בַמֶּה נֶחְשָׁב הֽוּא (Yeshayahu 2:22), הֲלוֹא נָכְרִיּוֹת נֶחְשַׁבְנוּ לוֹ (Bereishis 31:15), לֹא יֵֽחָשֵׁב לוֹ פִּגּוּל יִֽהְיֶה (Vayikra 7:18), and רְפָאִים יֵחָֽשְׁבוּ אַף־הֵם כַּֽעֲנָקִים (Devarim 2:11), the Refaim too were accounted Anakim.

קטף.sense: To pluck or crop off; of them all he says their sense is a sense of cutting.

more.t: אֵת רֹאשׁ יְנִֽיקוֹתָיו קָטָף (Yechezkel 17:4), he cropped off the top of its young shoots; וְקָֽטַפְתָּ מְלִילֹת (Devarim 23:26), you may pluck ears of grain; מֵרֹאשׁ יֹֽנְקוֹתָיו רַךְ אֶקְטֹף (Yechezkel 17:22), from the top of its shoots I will crop off a tender one; and in the passive עֹדֶנּוּ בְאִבּוֹ לֹא יִקָּטֵף (Iyov 8:12), while it is still in its greenness it is not plucked. Of all of them: ענינם ענין כריתה, their sense is a sense of cutting.

דוד.sense: An uncle, the father's brother; a beloved; a pot; a basket; and the דּוּדָאִים, mandrakes.

more.t: דּוֹד שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 10:14), Shaul's uncle, which he glosses as אחי אביו, his father's brother; לִבְנֵי דֹֽדֵיהֶן (Bamidbar 36:11), to the sons of אחי אביהן, their father's brothers; and דֹּדָֽתְךָ הִֽוא (Vayikra 18:14), she is אשת אחי אביך, your father's brother's wife.

לְעֵינֵי חֲנַמְאֵל דֹּדִי (Yirmiyahu 32:12) means the son of my uncle, this being the way of the Hebrews, as וְגַם אֶת־לוֹט אָחִיו (Bereishis 14:16), and also Lot his brother, means his brother's son. Or it may be that this was a different Chanamel who really was his uncle and was present at the purchase, since the Chanamel who sold was the son of Shallum, and Shallum was Yirmiyahu's uncle, while this one present at the purchase was his uncle, his father's brother. So Targum Yonasan rendered it, לְעֵינֵי חֲנַמְאֵל אַחֲבִי, before Chanamel my father's brother.

דּוֹדִי לי ואני לו (Shir HaShirim 2:16), which he glosses as ידידי ואהובי, my dear one and my beloved; כִּֽי־טוֹבִים דֹּדֶיךָ (Shir HaShirim 1:2), אהביך וידידותיך, your loves and endearments; so אֶתֵּן אֶת־ דֹּדַי לָֽךְ (Shir HaShirim 7:13) and נִרְוֶה דֹדִים עַד־הַבֹּקֶר (Mishlei 7:18).

בַכִּיּוֹר אוֹ בַדּוּד (Shmuel I 2:14), in the basin or in the pot; כַּפָּיו מִדּוּד תַּֽעֲבֹֽרְנָה (Tehillim 81:7); and וַיָּשִׂימוּ אֶת־רָֽאשֵׁיהֶם בַּדּוּדִים (Melachim II 10:7). The vav is given a vowel in בַּסִּירוֹת וּבַדְּוָדִים (Divrei HaYamim II 35:13); the sense of all of them is pots. In שְׁנֵי דּֽוּדָאֵי תְאֵנִים (Yirmiyahu 24:1), two baskets of figs, the alef is added, as the alef of לֻֽלָאֹת חֲמִשִּׁים (Shemos 36:17), fifty loops, is added, the pasuk saying afterwards הדּוּד אחד, the one basket, without it; their sense is baskets. He holds that וישימו את ראשיהם בדודים may be the same, בסלים, in baskets.

הַֽדּוּדָאִים נָֽתְנוּ־רֵיחַ (Shir HaShirim 7:14), the dudaim gave off their scent; וַיִּמְצָא דֽוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה (Bereishis 30:14); and בְּדֽוּדָאֵי בְּנִי (Bereishis 30:16). The alef in them may be an addition, or they may be another root altogether. They are the root of a plant shaped like a man, male and female, called mandragores in the vernacular.

ערס.sense: Dough: רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵכֶם, the first of your dough. Of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵכֶם (Bamidbar 15:20) and וְרֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֽוֹתֵיכֶם (Yechezkel 44:30), of which he says פירושו בצק, its meaning is dough, והוא ידוע, and it is known.

צפר.sense: To rise early, and so the morning; a winding round; צִפּוֹר, a bird; צָפִיר, a he-goat; and צִפֹּרֶן, a nail, and an iron stylus.

more.t: יָשֹׁב וְיִצְפֹּר (Shoftim 7:3), which he glosses as ישכים בבקר, let him rise early in the morning, since the Targum of בֹּקֶר, morning, is צַפְרָא. So בָּאָה הַצְּפִירָה (Yechezkel 7:7) is the decree that comes upon you in the morning.

Others explain both וְיִצְפֹּר and הַצְּפִירָה as a sense of going round, and Yonasan renders הַצְּפִירָה as מַלְכוּתָא, kingdom. On that reading וְלִצְפִירַת תִּפְאָרָה (Yeshayahu 28:5) is the turban wound round the head; and the Mishnah in Keilim has הקופה משיעשה בה שתי צפירות לרחב שלה, a basket from when two windings are made round its breadth, והערק משיעשה בה צפירה אחת, and the strap from when one winding is made in it, which he explains as the winding made round a basket.

כָּל־ צִפּוֹר טְהֹרָה (Devarim 14:11), every clean bird; כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל־כָּנָף (Yechezkel 17:23); and שְׁתֵּֽי־ צִפֳּרִים חַיּוֹת טְהֹרוֹת (Vayikra 14:4). In the masculine, כְּצִפּוֹר בּוֹדֵד עַל־גָּֽג (Tehillim 102:8), like a lone bird on a roof, and אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם צִפֳּרִים יְקַנֵּנוּ (Tehillim 104:17). It is a name covering every bird, but sometimes a particular one: in גַּם־ צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ (Tehillim 84:4), the bird too has found a house and the swallow a nest, the second word is particular and so the first is particular too, a small bird; and because its kind is so numerous, every bird came to be called by its name.

וְהַצָּפִיר הַשָּׂעִיר (Daniel 8:21), וּצְפִיר הָֽעִזִּים (Daniel 8:8), and צְפִירֵי חַטָּאת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר (Ezra 8:35), twelve he-goats for a sin offering; the word, he says, is known, and the Targum of שְׂעִיר (Bereishis 37:31) is צְפִיר. The doubling in וְהַצָּפִיר הַשָּׂעִיר is to make the sense plain, as in נֶגְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (Shemos 26:18) and קֵדְמָה מִזְרָֽחָה (Bamidbar 34:15), where the second word explains the first, since צפיר is not common in the language as שעיר is but belongs to Aramaic. Or else השעיר is from וְיִשְׂתָּעֵר עָלָיו מֶלֶךְ הַצָּפוֹן (Daniel 11:40), the king of the north will storm against him.

more.h: The nail, and the iron stylus
more.t: בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר (Yirmiyahu 17:1) and וְעָֽשְׂתָה אֶת־ צִפָּרְנֶֽיהָ (Devarim 21:12), she shall do her nails; the word is known. Since a man digs with his nails, the iron pen that digs was called a ציפורן, and so the pasuk says בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר, for שמיר is the hard iron; and the Midrash likewise has נטל צפורן של ברזל, he took an iron stylus.

כנף.sense: A wing; and by borrowing the corner or edge of a garment, the ends of the earth, the spreading of light, and being gathered in.

more.t: כָּל־בַּעַל כָּנָֽף (Mishlei 1:17), every owner of a wing, and כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל־ כָּנָֽף (Bereishis 7:14), which he glosses as כל צפור בעל כנף, every bird that owns a wing. So כְּנַף ־רְנָנִים נֶעֱלָסָה (Iyov 39:13), וְלָהֵנָּה כְנָפַיִם כְּכַנְפֵי הַֽחֲסִידָה (Zecharyah 5:9), they had wings like the wings of a stork, יִפְרֹשׂ כְּנָפָיו (Devarim 32:11), he spreads his wings, and כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה נֶחְפָּה בַכֶּסֶף (Tehillim 68:14). The sense, he says, is known.

By borrowing, אֲשֶׁר־בָּאת לַֽחֲסוֹת תַּֽחַת־ כְּנָפָֽיו (Rus 2:12), you came to take shelter under His wings, which is to shelter in His shade. The lower edge of a garment is called a כנף: עַל־צִיצִת הַכָּנָף (Bamidbar 15:38), on the fringe of the corner; על ארבע כַּנְפוֹת כסותך (Devarim 22:12), on the four corners of your covering; and וְנָגַע בִּכְנָפוֹ אֶל־הַלֶּחֶם (Chaggai 2:12), if he touches his garment's fold to bread.

מִכְּנַף הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 24:16) and לֶאֱחֹז בְּכַנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ (Iyov 38:13) are בקצות הארץ, at the ends of the earth; and אֶשָּׂא כַנְפֵי־שָׁחַר (Tehillim 139:9) means: if I go to the far end of the east.

וּמַרְפֵּא בִּכְנָפֶיהָ (Malachi 3:20), healing in its wings, likens the spreading of light to the spreading of a wing; and וְעַל כְּנַף שִׁקּוּצִים מְשֹׁמֵם (Daniel 9:27) he takes as: over the spreading of abominations a man will be appalled and full of wrath. In וְלֹֽא־ יִכָּנֵף עוֹד מוֹרֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 30:20) the verb means לא יאסף ולא יעצר, he will not be gathered away nor shut off, and the like of it is in Chazal's language, who call the gathering of a people and their assembling כנופיא (Yoma 51a). Some explain it as: he will not be far off, that is, will not be at the wing of the earth; and he has explained it under the root יָרָה.

אנה.sense: To mourn; to bring a thing about and cause it to come to hand, and to seek occasion against a man; and אֳנִי, a ship.

more.t: וְאָנוּ הַדַּיָּגִים (Yeshayahu 19:8), the fishermen mourn, and וְאָנוּ וְאָֽבְלוּ פְּתָחֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 3:26), her gates mourn and are in grief. The noun is תַּֽאֲנִיָּה וַֽאֲנִיָּֽה (Eichah 2:5), mourning and lament, and he calls the sense ענין אבל, a sense of mourning.

אִנָּה לְיָדוֹ (Shemos 21:13), where Hashem brought it about to his hand; and turned back on itself, כִּֽי־ מִתְאַנֶּה הוּא לִֽי (Melachim II 5:6), he is seeking an occasion against me. The noun is כִּי־ תֹאֲנָה הֽוּא־מְבַקֵּשׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shoftim 14:4), he was seeking an occasion from the Pelishtim, and in another form תַּֽאֲנָתָהּ מִי יְשִׁיבֶנָּה (Yirmiyahu 2:24). Their sense is ענין גרם הדבר וסבובו, a thing's being caused and brought round.

בַּל־תֵּלֶךְ בּוֹ אֳנִי ־שַׁיִט (Yeshayahu 33:21), no rowing ship will go on it, and אַחַת לְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים תָּבוֹא אֳנִי תַרְשִׁישׁ נֹֽשְׂאֵת זָהָב וָכֶסֶף (Melachim I 10:22), once in three years the ships of Tarshish came bearing gold and silver. In the masculine, אֳנִי חִירָם אֲשֶׁר־נָשָׂא זָהָב מֵֽאוֹפִיר (Melachim I 10:11); with the feminine heh, וְהָאֳנִיָּה חִשְּׁבָה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר (Yonah 1:4); and in the plural, אֳנִיּוֹת אֵבֶה (Iyov 9:26). Their sense is ספינה, a ship.

בכר.sense: Firstborn, and the right of the firstborn; the first-ripe fruit, בִּכּוּרִים; a woman bearing her first child; and young camels.

more.t: בְּכוֹר אֶתְּנֵהוּ (Tehillim 89:28), I will make him a firstborn. The plural comes both in the feminine way, מִבְּכֹרוֹת צֹאנוֹ (Bereishis 4:4), of the firstlings of his flock, and in the masculine, וְאֶת־בְּכוֹרֵי בְקָרֵינוּ (Nechemiah 10:37), the firstborn of our herds. From the same is the feminine הַבְּכִירָה (Bereishis 19:31), the elder daughter, בָּכִיר standing on the pattern of שָֹכיר, a hired man.

לָֽחֳדָשָׁיו יְבַכֵּר (Yechezkel 47:12), which he glosses ישא בכורים, it will bear first fruits; and לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר (Devarim 21:16), which he glosses לתת לו משפט הבכורה, to give him the right of the firstborn. In the passive, אֲשֶׁר יְבֻכַּר (Vayikra 27:26), what is made a firstling.

רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ (Shemos 23:19), the first of the first fruits of your ground; תְּאֵנִים עִם־בִּכּוּרִים (Nachum 3:12), figs with their first ripe fruit; and with a feminine ending, כְּבִכּוּרָה בִתְאֵנָה (Hoshea 9:10), like a first-ripe fig, and כִּתְאֵנֵי הַבַּכֻּרוֹת (Yirmiyahu 24:2), like first-ripe figs. Of them all he says ענינם ידוע, their sense is known, and it is the first fruit.
צָרָה כְּמַבְכִּירָה (Yirmiyahu 4:31), distress like hers who bears her first child, since her pangs are the stronger.

At Iyov 18:13. The angel set over death is called בְּכוֹר מָֽוֶת, firstborn of death, because he has a great portion in death; or death before its time is so called. His father explains it as the first illness to come upon a man, of which he dies, or as a phrase turned about, בכור בדיו, the firstborn of his branches, meaning that death eats his sons. And בְּכוֹרֵי דַלִּים (Yeshayahu 14:30) he takes of Yisrael, who have a portion of the firstborn and a great portion in poverty.

בִּכְרָה קַלָּה (Yirmiyahu 2:23), a swift young camel, and בִּכְרֵי מִדְיָן וְעֵיפָה (Yeshayahu 60:6): the young of the camels, male and female. The Targum renders the one הוֹגְנֵי מִדְיָן, the sucklings of Midyan, and the other יַנְקָא קַלִילָא, a swift suckling, since הוגני in the plural means sucklings and little ones, as Chazal say of the old camels that carry the hides of the young.

סכך.sense: To cover over and to screen; from it the סֻכָּה, a booth, and the מָסָךְ, the screen of an entrance; and separately סָךְ, a count.

more.t: סֹֽכְכִים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם (Shemos 25:20), covering with their wings, and כְּרוּב הַסֹּכֵךְ (Yechezkel 28:16), the covering keruv; יְסֻכֻּהוּ צֶאֱלִים (Iyov 40:22), the shady trees cover him. The same word is written with a sin at וְשַׂכֹּתִי כַפִּי (Shemos 33:22), and I will cover with My palm. Where the verb takes an object, בְּאֶבְרָתוֹ יָסֶךְ לָךְ (Tehillim 91:4), He will cover you with His pinion, and וַיָּסֶךְ בִּדְלָתַיִם יָם (Iyov 38:8), He shut in the sea with doors.

Most of the root, he says, is סיכוך למעלה, covering from above; but part of it is a partition and shield that divides one thing from another. So וְסַכֹּתָ עַל־הָֽאָרֹן אֶת־הַפָּרֹֽכֶת (Shemos 40:3), you shall screen the aron with the paroches, since the paroches was not over the aron but beside it, dividing between it and the ohel moed; and so פָּרֹכֶת הַמָּסָֽךְ (Shemos 35:12), the screening paroches, and מָסַךְ הַפֶּתַח (Shemos 35:15), the screen of the entrance.

וְסֻכָּה תִּהְיֶה לְצֵל־יוֹמָם מֵחֹרֶב (Yeshayahu 4:6), a booth for shade by day from the heat, and בַּסֻּכֹּת תֵּֽשְׁבוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים (Vayikra 23:42), you shall dwell in booths seven days. With an added mem, פָּרַשׂ עָנָן לְמָסָךְ (Tehillim 105:39), He spread a cloud for a screen; its proper form, he says, is מִסְכָךְ, on the pattern of מִכְלָל.

וְהֻכַן הַסֹּכֵֽךְ (Nachum 2:6), the covering is made ready: boards with hides over them, under which those attacking a city come up to the wall and dig beneath it, shielded from the stones thrown down on them from above.

The מוּסַךְ, the covering, of Melachim II 16:18. He holds the form is like מוֹרָֽד (Melachim I 7:29), whose root is רָדַד, the one being with shuruk and the other with cholam but the two being one. Rabbi Yonah explained it מחסה המשמרה, the shelter of the watch, the place where the men of the watch take cover. Yonasan renders it טִיקוּס, a word he leaves as it stands. Rashi wrote that it is the roof of a tent made for shade, to sit under in the azarah on Shabbos.

כִּי אֶֽעֱבֹר בַּסָּךְ (Tehillim 42:5), which he glosses במנין הקהל, in the count of the congregation and in the whole of it. Chazal speak the same way of a total, סך הכל (Avodah Zarah 11b), the sum of it all, and with a mem added, סכום מקח (Beitzah 29b), the sum of a purchase.

אלף.sense: A thousand; an אַלּוּף, a chief and a great man; to learn and to teach; and אֲלָפִים, oxen.

more.t: אֶלֶף לַמַּטֶּה (Bamidbar 31:4), a thousand to a tribe, and שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים (Shemos 18:21), captains of thousands, of which he says ענינם ידוע, their sense is known. From the same sense, צֹאונֵנוּ מַֽאֲלִיפוֹת (Tehillim 144:13), which he glosses יולדות לאלפים, bearing by the thousands.

אַלּוּפִי וּמְיֻדָּֽעִי (Tehillim 55:14), my familiar friend, אַלּוּף נְעֻרַי אָֽתָּה (Yirmiyahu 3:4), the chief of my youth, and אַלּוּף תֵּימָן אַלּוּף אוֹמָר (Bereishis 36:15). The sense of all of them is שר וגדול, a prince and a great man. Chazal (Sanhedrin 99b) said כל אלוף מלכותא בלא תגא, every aluf is kingship without a crown, for a man is called king when he is crowned and aluf when he is not.

Some read הִנֵּה אַלְפִּי הַדַּל בִּמְנַשֶּׁה (Shoftim 6:15) from the sense of a chief, taking it as my father, and what follows proves it: וְאָֽנֹכִי הַצָּעִיר בְּבֵית אָבִֽי, and I am the youngest in my father's house. On the same footing they read וְצֵלַע הָאֶלֶף (Yehoshua 18:28) as the great one. Yonasan read כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף (Yirmiyahu 11:19) from it, rendering כְּאִימֵר בְּחִיר, like a choice lamb.

פֶּן־תֶּאֱלַף (Mishlei 22:25), lest you learn his ways; and where the verb takes an object, כִּֽי־יְאַלֵּף עֲוֹֽנְךָ פִיךָ (Iyov 15:5), which he glosses כי ילמד עונך פיך, your sin teaches your mouth; וַֽאֲאַלֶּפְךָ חָכְמָֽה (Iyov 33:33), and I will teach you wisdom; and מַלְּפֵנוּ מִבַּֽהֲמוֹת אָרֶץ (Iyov 35:11), teaching us from the beasts of the earth, whose proper form is מְאַלְּפֵנוּ.

At Shir HaShirim 4:4. Some read it from this root with the alef dropped for ease, the full form being לְתַֽאַלְפִּיּוֹת. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the tav stands in place of the alef, so that it is as אַלְפִּיּוֹת and means teaching: the tower is high, and so a thing that wayfarers are taught by. He himself takes it for a compound word and sets it at root תלל.

שְׁגַר־אֲלָפֶיךָ (Devarim 7:13) and וְהָֽאֲלָפִים וְהָֽעֲיָרִים (Yeshayahu 30:24) are oxen. In another form, אַלּוּפֵינוּ מְֽסֻבָּלִים (Tehillim 144:14), our oxen laden, either laden with flesh, that is, fat and full of meat, or laden with work, there being much to work with them. In כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף יוּבַל לִטְבוֹחַ (Yirmiyahu 11:19) a kaf of comparison or an added vav is wanting: like a lamb, like an ox, or like a lamb and an ox led to the slaughter.

בקר.sense: To seek out and examine; from this the morning, בֹּקֶר, when everything is made out by daylight; and separately בָּקָר, cattle.

more.t: וְדָֽרַשְׁתִּי אֶת־צֹאנִי וּבִקַּרְתִּֽים (Yechezkel 34:11), I will seek out My flock and look them over; לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּר הַכֹּהֵן (Vayikra 13:36), the kohen shall not examine; and יִֽהְיֶה־לִּי לְבַקֵּֽר (Melachim II 16:15), which he glosses כשיעלה בלבי לבקרו, when it comes into my heart to inspect it. The noun is כְּבַקָּרַת רֹעֶה עֶדְרוֹ (Yechezkel 34:12), like a shepherd's looking over his flock. All of them, he says, are דרישה ובקור, seeking and examining.

Because in the morning every thing is made out by the light of day, while its opposite, the evening, is when all things mix together and a man cannot tell them apart. So the light itself is called בקר: כּוֹכְבֵי בֹקֶר (Iyov 38:7), stars of the morning, as though he had said stars of light, like כָּל־כּוֹכְבֵי אֽוֹר (Tehillim 148:3), and those, he says, are the seven that serve. And the morning is called אור: מִן־הָאוֹר עַד־מַֽחֲצִית הַיּוֹם (Nechemiah 8:3), from the light until midday, as though he had said from the morning. On that footing וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלֽוֹ (Tehillim 27:4) may be read as ולשחר, to seek Him at dawn.

At Vayikra 19:20, which he glosses מולקת תהיה, she shall be lashed. Rav Saadiah Gaon wrote that the word is בקורת because the lashes are given with רצועה של בקר, a strap of cattle hide; or the bet stands in place of a peh, the two letters being near because they come from one place in the mouth, as the Mishnah's הבקר לעניים (Peah 6:1), declared free for the poor, is as הפקר, ownerless. Targum Yerushalmi renders וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ (Shemos 23:11) with ותבקרון יתה, you shall leave it free. So the sense here is that she is as ownerless, not having been freed, and therefore they are not put to death, though there is lashing. Chazal hold the lashing is hers and not his, since the pasuk says תִּֽהְיֶה and not יהיו.

צֹאן־וּבָקָר (Bereishis 13:5), flocks and herds, whose sense he calls known; in the plural, אִם־יַֽחֲרוֹשׁ בַּבְּקָרִים (Amos 6:12), does one plough with oxen. And the verb כִּֽי־בוֹקֵר אָנֹכִי (Amos 7:14), which he glosses רועה הבקר, a herdsman of cattle.

גבן.sense: Cheese, גְּבִנָּה, and no more; of its sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: One pasuk, הֲלֹא כֶֽחָלָב תַּתִּיכֵנִי וְכַגְּבִנָּה תַּקְפִּיאֵֽנִי (Iyov 10:10), did You not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese, of which he says ידוע, its sense is known. Rabbi Yonah brought אֽוֹ־גִבֵּן אוֹ־דַק (Vayikra 21:20) and הָרִים גַּבְנֻנִּים (Tehillim 68:17) under this root; he has written them at root גב, and holds that the right place.

חרץ.sense: Moving, and so being diligent; decreeing and giving judgment; cutting, and so a threshing sledge, a trench and cheeses; and gold.

more.t: לֹֽא־חָרַץ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאִישׁ אֶת־לְשֹׁנֽוֹ (Yehoshua 10:21), which he glosses as: not one of them moved his tongue against Yisrael, the lamed of לאיש being an extra one like the lamed of הַשְּׁלִשִׁי לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם (Divrei HaYamim I 3:2); or it means to a man of Bnei Yisrael, that not one of them moved his tongue even at a single man, and all the less at all of them together. So too לֹא יֶֽחֱרַץ־כֶּלֶב לְשֹׁנוֹ (Shemos 11:7), no dog shall move its tongue, and אָז תֶּחֱרָץ (Shmuel II 5:24). The sense of these is ענין התנועה, movement.

מַחְשְׁבוֹת חָרוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָר (Mishlei 21:5), the thoughts of the diligent are only to profit. וְהֽוֹן־אָדָם יָקָר חָרֽוּץ (Mishlei 12:27) he reads as though turned about, והון אדם חרוץ יקר, the wealth of a diligent man is precious; and some take חרוץ there for a noun, so that the precious thing in a man's wealth is החריצות, diligence itself. In the plural, וְיַד חָרֽוּצִים תַּֽעֲשִֽׁיר (Mishlei 10:4), the hand of the diligent makes rich, and וְנֶפֶשׁ חָֽרֻצִים תְּדֻשָּֽׁן (Mishlei 13:4). They are men who bestir themselves after their food and do their work in uprightness and justice, quick to acquire this world and the next, the opposite of the lazy and the deceitful.

כֵּן מִשְׁפָּטֶךָ אַתָּה חָרָֽצְתָּ (Melachim I 20:40), so is your judgment, you yourself have decreed it; בְּעֵמֶק הֶֽחָרוּץ (Yoel 4:14), which the Targum renders בְּמֵישַׁר פִּלוּג דִינָא, the plain where judgment is divided; כִּי כָלָה וְנֶחֱרָצָה (Yeshayahu 10:23), which he reads as: and the destruction is decreed; and אִם חֲרוּצִים יָמָיו (Iyov 14:5), if his days are cut out for him, the form being a passive one, גזורים, decreed.

כִּי לֹא בֶֽחָרוּץ יוּדַשׁ קֶצַח (Yeshayahu 28:27), for black cumin is not threshed with a חרוץ, as in הִנֵּה שַׂמְתִּיךְ לְמוֹרַג חָרוּץ חָדָשׁ (Yeshayahu 41:15). It is a board of wood with fine stones set under it, to cut the straw and bring the grain out of its husk; the tool's name is מורג, and it is called חרוץ for the work it does. Either מורג and חרוץ differ somewhat though they are one tool, or חרוץ describes the מורג as one that cuts well, and such a great heavy tool is not fit for threshing קצח, black cumin, and fine seed.

וּבַֽחֲרִצֵי הַבַּרְזֶל (Shmuel II 12:31) and בַּֽחֲרֻצוֹת הַבַּרְזֶל (Amos 1:3), the sense of all of them being החתוך והכריתה, cutting and severing. So אֽוֹ־חָר֣וּץ אֽוֹ־יַבֶּ֗לֶת (Vayikra 22:22), which they explained as cut, and which Chazal take of an eyelid split or nicked, or a lip split or nicked. And וְנִבְנְתָה רְחוֹב וְחָרוּץ (Daniel 9:25) is a trench dug in the ground, as the Mishnah's חריץ שבין שתי חצרות (Eruvin 7:3), a trench between two courtyards.

חֲרִצֵי הֶֽחָלָב (Shmuel I 17:18), which the Targum renders גוּבְנִין דַחֲלָבָא, cheeses of milk; he suggests they are so named because they are pressed in the making, and the work resembles the work of the חרוץ in threshing. And מֵחָרוּץ וּמִפָּז (Mishlei 8:19), בִּֽירַקְרַק חָרֽוּץ (Tehillim 68:14) and וְחָרוּץ כְּטִיט חוּצֽוֹת (Zechariah 9:3) are all of them gold, though some explain precious stones. Rabbi Yonah wrote that וְיַד חָרֽוּצִים תַּֽעֲשִֽׁיר (Mishlei 10:4) may be from this too, meaning the great merchants who deal in gold.

כסס.sense: Counting: תָּכֹסּוּ עַל־הַשֶּֽׂה, you shall make your count for the lamb; and the מֶכֶס, the tax, is named from number.

more.t: תָּכֹסּוּ עַל־הַשֶּֽׂה (Shemos 12:4), you shall make your count for the lamb, and in the same pasuk בְּמִכְסַת נְפָשֹׁת, by the number of souls; אֵת מִכְסַת הָֽעֶרְכְּךָ (Vayikra 27:23), the sum of your valuation; and in another form וַיְהִי הַמֶּכֶס (Bamidbar 31:37). All of them, he says, are ענין מנין, a sense of number.

more.h: Why the tax is called מֶכֶס
more.t: It is named from number, because those who take the tax take by number from the one who passes them, a fifth or a sixth or a tenth, according to the law and the custom.

more.h: The mem becomes a root letter
more.t: Chazal used the word so much, as in היה עובר על בית המכס (Kilayim 9:3), one who was passing the tax house, that they fixed the mem as a root letter and called the collectors מוכסים: אין פורטין מתיבת המוכסים (Bava Kamma 113a), one does not change money out of the collectors' chest. So too they fixed the tav of תְּחִלָּה and said מַתְחִיל, he begins, and the tav of תְּרוּמָה and said תּוֹרֵם, he separates terumah.

גזל.sense: To rob and to seize, with גֵּזֶל for the robbery; and separately גּוֹזָל, a fledgling, the young of the dove.

more.t: וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת־הַגְּזֵלָה אֲשֶׁר גָּזָל (Vayikra 5:23), he shall return the robbed thing that he robbed, and אֲשֶׁר גָּֽזְלוּ עַבְדֵי אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ (Bereishis 21:25); of people too, פֶּן־תִּגְזֹל אֶת־בְּנוֹתֶיךָ מֵֽעִמִּֽי (Bereishis 31:31), lest you seize your daughters from me. In the passive, וְֽנִגְזְלָה שְׁנָתָם (Mishlei 4:16), their sleep is robbed from them. The noun is בְגָזֵל (Vayikra 5:21), by robbery, and in the construct גֵּזֶל אָח (Yechezkel 18:18), a brother's robbery, and וְגֵזֶל מִשְׁפָּט וָצֶדֶק (Koheles 5:7), the robbing of justice and right. Of these he says ענינם ידוע, their sense is known.

וְתֹר וְגוֹזָֽל (Bereishis 15:9), a turtledove and a young bird: it is the young of the dove, and גוֹזָֽל means the small bird, as עַל־גּֽוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֶף (Devarim 32:11), it hovers over its young; for of the doves only the small ones are fit for a korban.

עצר.sense: To restrain, shut up or hold back, and so to detain; from it rule, which holds the people in check, and עֲצָרָה, an assembly held in one place.

more.t: וְעָצַר אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם (Devarim 11:17), and He shuts up the heavens, and הֵן יַעְצֹר בַּמַּיִם וְיִבָשׁוּ (Iyov 12:15), He holds back the waters and they dry up. In the passive, וְהַמַּגֵּפָה נֶֽעֱצָֽרָה (Bamidbar 17:15), the plague was stayed. The noun is שְׁאוֹל וְעֹצֶר רָחַם (Mishlei 30:16).

כִּי אִם־אִשָּׁה עֲצֻֽרָה (Shmuel I 21:6) he takes as מנועה ממנו, withheld from us, held back on our account, she not having been with us as before since he went out. The bread itself carries no me'ilah, since there is none in the lechem hapanim once the bezichin have been burned; and even the loaves still on the shulchan, which the shulchan makes holy, they could eat, since there was no other bread and they were hungry, and nothing stands before pikuach nefesh but avodah zarah, gilui arayos and shefichus damim. So it appears to him from Chazal in Menachos 95b, and he notes that he explained the pasuk otherwise under the root חָלַל.

In a neighbouring sense the word is holding up. וְלֹא עָצַרְתִּי כֹּֽחַ (Daniel 10:8) he reads as לא עכבתי הכח לעצמי, I kept no strength back for myself; וְלֹא עָֽצְרוּ לָלֶכֶת אֶל־תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ (Divrei HaYamim II 20:37) as they had no strength to go to Tarshish; and אַל־ תַּֽעֲצָר ־לִי לִרְכֹּב (Melachim II 4:24) as אל תעכב לי הבהמה לרכוב, do not hold the animal back from me to ride. So נַעְצְרָה ־נָּא אוֹתָךְ (Shoftim 13:15), let us detain you, and עוֹדֶנּוּ עָצוּר בַּֽחֲצַר הַמַּטָּרָה (Yirmiyahu 33:1), he was still shut up in the court of the guard.

more.h: What is shut in and what is left out
more.t: On עָצוּר וְעָזוּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim I 14:10), and on וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזֽוּב (Devarim 32:37), his father takes עָצוּר as the wealth shut up in the houses and עָזוּב as the cattle left out in the field.

more.h: Rule, which holds the people in
more.t: Kingship and dominion are called עֶצֶר, as יוֹרֵשׁ עֶצֶר (Shoftim 18:7), an heir to rule, and זֶה יַעְצֹר בְּעַמִּֽי (Shmuel I 9:17), this one shall hold sway over My people, because the king or the ruler restrains the people from going out and from doing anything without his leave, in the manner of וּבִלְעָדֶיךָ לֹֽא־יָרִים אִישׁ אֶת־יָדוֹ וְאֶת־רַגְלוֹ (Bereishis 41:44), without you no man shall lift his hand or his foot.

A gathering of men in one place is called עֲצָרָה, as קַדְּשׁוּ־צוֹם קִרְאוּ עֲצָרָה (Yoel 1:14), sanctify a fast, call an assembly, because they are held and stay in the place of their gathering. His father explains עֲצֶרֶת בֹּֽגְדִֽים (Yirmiyahu 9:1) as a kingdom of traitors, from יוֹרֵשׁ עֶצֶר, an heir to rule. The festival is called עֲצֶרֶת because the people are held back in it from doing work, and the eighth day of Sukkos is the one called עצרת on its own (Divrei HaYamim II 7:9), either because it had nothing to be named by, as chag hamatzos and chag hashavuos and chag hasukkos have, or because the olei regel were held there after they had finished Sukkos, to keep that day holy.

המה.sense: To make a noise: nations in tumult, innards moaning, bears and dogs and doves, the sound of a harp, and a city loud with it.

more.t: הָמוּ גוֹיִם מָטוּ מַמְלָכוֹת (Tehillim 46:7), the nations were in tumult, the kingdoms tottered; עַל־כֵּן הָמוּ מֵעַי (Yirmiyahu 31:19), therefore my innards moan; נֶהֱמֶה כַדֻּבִּים כֻּלָּנוּ (Yeshayahu 59:11), we all growl like bears; כְּיוֹנֵי הַגֵּֽאָיוֹת כֻּלָּם הֹמוֹת (Yechezkel 7:16), like the doves of the valleys, all of them moaning; יָשׁוּבוּ לָעֶרֶב יֶהֱמוּ כַכָּלֶב (Tehillim 59:7), they return at evening and howl like a dog; and לִבִּי לְמוֹאָב כַּֽחֲלִלִים יֶֽהֱמֶה (Yirmiyahu 48:36), my heart sounds for Moav like flutes.

עִיר הֽוֹמִיָּה קִרְיָה עַלִּיזָה (Yeshayahu 22:2), a noisy city, a joyous town; בְּרֹאשׁ הֹֽמִיּוֹת תִּקְרָא (Mishlei 1:21), she calls at the head of the noisy streets; and מַדּוּעַ קֽוֹל־הַקִּרְיָה הוֹמָֽה (Melachim I 1:41), why is the sound of the city in an uproar.

כַּֽהֲמוֹת יַמִּים (Yeshayahu 17:12), like the roaring of seas; הֶמְיַת נְבָלֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 14:11), the sound of your harps; and הֲמוֹן שִׁירָיִךְ (Amos 5:23), the noise of your songs. Their sense, he says, he set out under the root הִים, in the second sense there.

more.h: A son who cries out under rebuke
more.t: Some take from this וְאֶל־ הֲמִיתוֹ אַל־תִּשָּׂא נַפְשֶֽׁךָ (Mishlei 19:18): chasten your son, and if he weeps and moans do not set your heart on him and do not let your soul pity him, this being the way of rebuke. On that reading הֲמִיתוֹ, his moaning, comes from הָמָה as בְּכִיתוֹ, his weeping, comes from בָּכָה.

more.h: A word others read as of this root
more.t: Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote that וְלֹֽא מֵהֱמֵהֶם (Yechezkel 7:11) is of this root and this sense, a noun הָמֶה on the pattern of קָשֶׁה, hard, and יָפֶה, fair, which with the plural suffix gives המהם as one would say קשהם, יפהם. Yonasan renders it וְלָא מִבְּנֵיהוֹן, and not of their sons.

מלל.sense: To speak or utter, with מִלָּה, a word; and separately מְלִילֹת, ears of grain a man rubs out in his hand.

more.t: מִי מִלֵּל לְאַבְרָהָם (Bereishis 21:7), who would have said to Avraham; בָּרוּר מִלֵּֽלוּ (Iyov 33:3), they uttered it clearly; and מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת (Tehillim 106:2), who can utter the mighty acts of Hashem. The Targum of וַיְדַבֵּר, and he spoke, is וּמַלִּיל.

אֵין מִלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנִי (Tehillim 139:4), there is no word on my tongue. The plural in the masculine is הַֽלְהוֹכַח מִלִּים תַּחְשֹׁבוּ (Iyov 6:26), do you think to reprove with words, and אַחְבִּירָה עֲלֵיכֶם בְּמִלִּים (Iyov 16:4), I would string words together against you; and at times it comes with a nun, אֲנִי אֲשִֽׁיבְךָ מִלִּין (Iyov 35:4) and הֲלֹא־אֹזֶן מִלִּין תִּבְחָן (Iyov 12:11), does not the ear test words.

more.h: A noise some read as a word
more.t: Some explain קוֹל הֲמֻלָּה (Yechezkel 1:24) as though it were מלה, a word, and so the Targum holds, which rendered it קָל מִלוּלֵיהֶן, the sound of their speech. He has already written it as a root of its own, under הָמַל.

By way of figure the light form gives מֹלֵל בְּרַגְלָו (Mishlei 6:13), he speaks with his feet, set beside קֹרֵץ בְּעֵינָו, he winks with his eyes, in the same pasuk: it is as though he speaks with his feet when he makes signs with them.

וְקָֽטַפְתָּ מְלִילֹת בְּיָדֶךָ (Devarim 23:26), and you may pluck ears with your hand. The sense of מלילה, rubbing out ears, is known from Chazal (Beitzah 12b): one who rubs out ears on erev Shabbos blows them the next day from one hand to the other and eats; and they said there too that one may rub out ears and crush pulse on Yom Tov.

רקם.sense: Embroidery: a garment worked in many colours, whether in the weaving or with the needle.

more.t: מַֽעֲשֵׂה רֹקֵֽם (Shemos 26:36), the work of an embroiderer; the noun is שְׁלַל צְבָעִים רִקְמָה (Shoftim 5:30), spoil of dyed stuffs, embroidered; and the plural לִרְקָמוֹת תּוּבַל (Tehillim 45:15), she is led in embroidered robes. Work of garments made of many colours, in the weaving or with the needle, is what is called רִקְמָה, embroidery.

more.h: Why the word comes in twos
more.t: צֶבַע רִקְמָתַיִם (Shoftim 5:30) stands in the form of two because it is embroidered on two faces, this side and that alike, or in two manners after the way of embroidery. So he speaks of the colours of the feather in הַנּוֹצָה אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הָֽרִקְמָה (Yechezkel 17:3).

more.h: A man embroidered in the womb
more.t: רֻקַּמְתִּי בְּֽתַחְתִּיּוֹת אָֽרֶץ (Tehillim 139:15), I was wrought in the lowest parts of the earth: he likens the forming of a man, in sinews and bones and flesh and skin, to the work of embroidery, and likens his mother's womb to the lowest parts of the earth, a place hidden and dark.

ערשֹ.sense: A bed, the thing a man lies on.

more.t: הִנֵּה עַרְשׂוֹ עֶרֶשׂ בַּרְזֶל (Devarim 3:11), his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; עַל־ עֶרֶשׂ דְּוָי (Tehillim 41:4), on a bed of sickness; אַף־ עַרְשֵׂנוּ רַֽעֲנָנָֽה (Shir HaShirim 1:16), our couch too is fresh and green; and the plural in the feminine, וּסְרֻחִים עַל־ עַרְשׂוֹתָם (Amos 6:4), sprawling on their couches. The Targum of מטה, a bed, is עַרְסָא.

עוג.sense: The עֻגָה, a cake baked on the coals, and the verb of baking it.

more.t: תְּעֻגֶנָה לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם (Yechezkel 4:12), you shall bake it before their eyes. The right form, he says, is תעוגנה with a dagesh in the nun, since the separate form is תָּעוּג אותה, you shall bake it, and the quiescent letter came in place of the dagesh. Some say כִּֽי־ תִקְרֶאנָה מִלְחָמָה (Shemos 1:10) comes the same way, the feminine suffix pointing at the city, that war should befall the city; and one may read תעוגנה of the women instead. The word is of baking the cake and not of kneading it, since they dry cattle dung and kindle it and bake with it.

הָיָה עֻגָה בְּלִי הֲפוּכָֽה (Hoshea 7:8): a cake baked on the coals and not turned is baked on one side only and is not fit to eat. So was Ephraim, who was hasty in his counsel and did not turn it over and settle whether it was sound.

וְעֻגַת שְׂעֹרִים תֹּֽאֽכֲלֶנָּה (Yechezkel 4:12), a barley cake you shall eat, and עֻגַת רְצָפִים (Melachim I 19:6), which he glosses as a cake baked on coals. Another form is אִם־יֶשׁ־לִי מָעוֹג (Melachim I 17:12), and of these he says only that their sense is known.

Others took בְּחַנְפֵי לַֽעֲגֵי מָעוֹג (Tehillim 35:16) in this sense, of a cake. In his own view it is a sense of mockery and idle words. He finds the like in Chazal (Sanhedrin 90a), where Abba Shaul says that one who pronounces the Name by its letters has no share in the World to Come, and the Gemara (101b) taught ובגבולין ובלשון עגה, in the provinces and in a tongue of agah: that is, if he mentions the Name in the provinces even at need, and in a tongue of mockery and idle words even in Yerushalayim.

עצד.sense: The מַֽעֲצָד, a craftsman's cutting tool; he leaves it between a large axe and a smaller implement.

more.t: חָרַשׁ בַּרְזֶל מַֽעֲצָד (Yeshayahu 44:12), the ironsmith with his maatzad, and מַֽעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי־חָרָשׁ בַּֽמַּֽעֲצָֽד (Yirmiyahu 10:3), the work of a craftsman's hands with the maatzad. It is the קרדום, the axe, or else one of two smaller tools he names in his own vernacular.

What forced him to the two is what he found of the word in Chazal. The Mishnah (Bava Kama 10:10) has that what the craftsman brings out with a מעצד is his own and what he brings out with a כשיל is the householder's; on its reckoning the מעצד is the small tool, one of the two he names, both of them small, and the כשיל is the large axe. The Baraisa has that what the craftsman brings out with a מעצד, and what is cut off with a saw, are the householder's; it did not mention the כשיל at all, because it called that tool a מעצד, so that on its reckoning the מעצד is the large axe.
What they said further (Arachin 23b), that if he was a craftsman they give him two מעצדין, is the large and the small, as he explained.

בוס.sense: To tread down and trample, and so to be befouled in mire or in blood; a few of its uses he reads instead as despising.

more.t: תָּבוּס נֹפֶת (Mishlei 27:7), which he takes as כמו תבוז, as though it were the word for spurning, the sated soul spurning the honeycomb; יָבוּס צָרֵֽינוּ (Tehillim 60:14), He will tread down our foes; and וְעַל־הָרַי אֲבוּסֶנּוּ (Yeshayahu 14:25), on My mountains I will trample him. So too כְּפֶגֶר מוּבָֽס (Yeshayahu 14:19), like a trodden carcass, which he reads as כמו מובז, as though it were the word for one despised. The noun is כִּי יוֹם מְהוּמָה וּמְבוּסָה (Yeshayahu 22:5), a day of tumult and treading down.

תְּבוּסַת אֲחַזְיָהוּ לָבוֹא אֶל־יוֹרָם (Divrei HaYamim II 22:7), Achazyahu's downfall in his coming to Yoram: it was from Hashem that it was put in his heart to go to Yoram, and in that going was his downfall, for Yehu did not deal with him as with a king but despised him and said to his servants גַּם־אֹתוֹ הַכֻּהוּ אֶל־הַמֶּרְכָּבָה (Melachim II 9:27), smite him also, in the chariot.

In the doubled form, בּֽוֹסְסוּ מִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ (Yeshayahu 63:18), they have trodden down Your Mikdash, and בֹּֽסְסוּ אֶת־חֶלְקָתִי (Yirmiyahu 12:10), they have trodden my portion. These may be כמו בזזו, as though the word were the one for plundering, or they are of treading and befouling, and that, he says, is the right one.

בּוֹסִים בְּטִיט חוּצוֹת (Zechariah 10:5) is an adjective of the light form, on the pattern of טוֹבִים, good, and בּוֹשִׁים, ashamed, and means befouled and trodden in the mire of the streets: the nations, who were as mighty men, will be trodden in the mire of the streets. Or בוסים is an adjective that takes an object, and the sense is that Israel will be as mighty men though they are weak, as it says after, וְהָיוּ כְגִבּוֹר אֶפְרַיִם (Zechariah 10:7), and Ephraim shall be as a mighty man: they will be treading and trampling their enemies in the mire of the streets in war, since Hashem is with them, and the nations, who are the riders of horses, will be put to shame.

The reflexive is מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת בְּדָמָיִךְ (Yechezkel 16:6), befouled in your blood. His father writes that יַעַן בּֽוֹשַׁסְכֶם עַל־דָּל (Amos 5:11), because you tread upon the poor, is of this root and this sense, with shin interchanging with sin, as וּבוֹלֵס שִׁקְמִֽים (Amos 7:14) stands for בולש, one who searches out sycamore figs, the Targum of וַיְחַפֵּשׂ, and he searched, being וּבְלַשׁ; and בושסכם would be of the four-letter form, on the pattern of כּוֹנַנְכֶם, your establishing.

סרף.sense: A man's mother's brother, where the דּוֹד is his father's brother; others take the word from burning instead.

more.t: On וּנְשָׂאוֹ דּוֹדוֹ וּמְסָֽרְפוֹ (Amos 6:10), his uncle and his mesarfo shall carry him, he says that the מְסָֽרְפוֹ is his mother's brother, since the דּוֹד is his father's brother. Some explain it from שריפה, burning, that is, the one who burned him, to bring the bones out of the house. Yonasan renders it וְיִטְלִנֵיהּ קְרִיבֵיהּ מִיְקֵידָא, his kinsman shall take him up out of the burning.

טבל.sense: To dip, which he sets beside washing: washing is to clean a thing, dipping is to bring it, part or whole, into what is wet.

more.t: וְטָבַל הַכֹּהֵן (Vayikra 4:6), the kohen shall dip; וַיִּטְבְּלוּ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּנֶת בַּדָּֽם (Bereishis 37:31), they dipped the coat in the blood; וְטָבַלְתְּ פִּתֵּךְ בַּחֹמֶץ (Rus 2:14), dip your morsel in the vinegar; וְטֹבֵל בַּשֶּׁמֶן רַגְלֽוֹ (Devarim 33:24), dipping his foot in oil; and וַיֵּרֶד וַיִּטְבֹּל בַּיַּרְדֵּן שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים (Melachim II 5:14), he went down and immersed in the Yarden seven times. In the passive, נִטְבְּלוּ בִּקְצֵה הַמָּיִם (Yehoshua 3:15), they were dipped at the edge of the water.

All of them are of the sense of רחיצה, washing, but there is a difference between them: washing is to clean the thing, while dipping is at times the touching of a thing to what is wet, part of it or the whole of it.

more.h: Dipped in the pit, dipped in dye
more.t: By way of figure, אָז בַּשַּׁחַת תִּטְבְּלֵנִי (Iyov 9:31): even were I washed in snow water You would dip me in the pit, that is, I shall not be saved from the pit. And סְרוּחֵי טְבוּלִים בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶם (Yechezkel 23:15) he says of the turbans on their heads, which hang long and loose behind them, טְבוּלִים meaning that the turbans are dipped in dye.

ידה.sense: To cast or throw; and in a second sense to give thanks and praise, from which תּוֹדָה, thanksgiving, the name יְהוּדָה, and confessing a sin.

more.t: יְדוּ אֵלֶיהָ (Yirmiyahu 50:14), which he glosses השליכו, cast at her; לְיַדּוֹת אֶת־קַרְנוֹת הַגּוֹיִם (Zechariah 2:5), to cast down the horns of the nations; and וַיַּדּוּ ־אֶבֶן בִּֽי (Eichah 3:52), they cast a stone at me, whose proper form is וַיְיַּדּוּ. Rabbi Yehudah said that גָּמוּל יָדוֹ הָדָֽה (Yeshayahu 11:8) is from this same source, with heh in place of yud. His father holds the verb is of the form that makes another act, its proper form being וְֽיַיְּדּוּ.

In the other form the sense is praise and thanksgiving: הוֹדִינוּ לְּךָ (Tehillim 75:2), we give thanks to You; גַּם־אֲנִי אוֹדְךָ בִכְלִי־נֶבֶל (Tehillim 71:22), I too will praise You with the harp; יוֹדוּ שִׁמְךָ גָּדוֹל וְנוֹרָא (Tehillim 99:3), let them praise Your name, great and awesome; and עַל־כֵּן עַמִּים יְהוֹדֻךָ (Tehillim 45:18), therefore peoples will praise You. The noun is תּוֹדָה וְקוֹל זִמְרָֽה (Yeshayahu 51:3), thanksgiving and the sound of song.

more.h: Yehudah, and why all Israel are Jews
more.t: The name is taken from it: עַל־כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ יְהוּדָה (Bereishis 29:35), therefore she called his name Yehudah. Since the mainstay of Israel's kingship and their strong horn was Yehudah, all Israel were called יהודים, Jews, as וְאֶל־ הַיְּהוּדִים כִּכְתָבָם (Esther 8:9), and to the Jews in their own script, and וְֽהֶחֱזִיקוּ בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי (Zechariah 8:23), they will take hold of the corner of a Jew's garment. The holy tongue was named for it too, וְאַל־תְּדַבֵּר אֵלֵינוּ יְהוּדִית (Yeshayahu 36:11), do not speak to us in Yehudis; and a verb was built from it for turning from the nations to the faith of the Jews, וְרַבִּים מֵֽעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִֽתְיַֽהֲדִים (Esther 8:17).

Another sense is confession: וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָֽם (Mishlei 28:13), one who confesses and forsakes will be shown mercy, and וְגַם־אֲנִי אוֹדֶךָּ (Iyov 40:14), though this last may be of the second sense instead. יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ (Bereishis 49:8) he reads as that they will acknowledge to you that you are fit to rule over them. The reflexive is וְהִתְוַדָּה אֲשֶׁר חָטָא עָלֶֽיהָ (Vayikra 5:5), he shall confess what he has sinned, and וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת־חַטָּאתָם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ (Bamidbar 5:7).

זְבַח לֵאלֹהִים תּוֹדָה (Tehillim 50:14): the offering over which a man confesses his sins is called תּוֹדָה, thanksgiving, but it did not carry the law of a chatas or an asham, only that of shelamim, and it was eaten for a day and a night alone. Though it came upon sins it was neither chatas nor asham, since those come for one particular sin, while a man brought this offering for all his sins together, when he wished to confess and return to the good way. Some say a man brought it when a nes was done for him, and that it is called תּוֹדָה because he was thanking Hashem for the nes done for him. So אִם עַל־ תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ (Vayikra 7:12).

שְׁתֵּי תוֹדֹת גְּדוֹלֹת (Nechemiah 12:31) are the two thanksgiving breads that were chametz, as עַל־ חַלֹּת לֶחֶם חָמֵץ יַקְרִיב קָרְבָּנוֹ (Vayikra 7:13) has it; they are called great because of the matzah there were three kinds and of the chametz one alone, so that the one kind stands against three. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yonah put שְׁתֵּי תוֹדֹת גְּדוֹלֹת and וְהַתּוֹדָה הַשֵּׁנִית (Nechemiah 12:38) in another sense, and Rabbi Yonah explained them as a term of assembly, a congregation and congregations.
