Chazal explained as he wrote: the Mishnah in Shevuos has that the city and the azaros are added to only with a beis din of seventy-one and with two todos and with song, the inner loaf eaten and the outer burned, and the Gemara taught that the two todos spoken of are in their bread and not in their flesh.

חמשׁ.sense: Five, and from it fifty and the fifth part; and men who go up חֲמֻשִׁים, girded with arms at the fifth rib.

more.t: וּמִקְצֵה אֶחָיו לָקַח חֲמִשָּׁה אֲנָשִׁים, from among his brothers he took five men, and in the feminine וְחָמֵשׁ צֹאן (Shmuel I 25:18), five sheep. The larger number is שַׂר־ חֲמִשִּׁים וַֽחֲמִשָּׁיו (Melachim II 1:9), a captain of fifty and his fifty, and וְאֶת־ חֲמִשֶּׁיךָ, which he glosses חמשים שלך, your fifty.

וַֽחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 13:18) he takes as חגורי חומש בכלי זין, girded at the chomesh with weapons, which is the fifth rib. So Chazal explained (Sanhedrin 49a) on וַיַּכֵּהוּ אַבְנֵר בְּאַֽחֲרֵי הַֽחֲנִית אֶל־ הַחֹמֶשׁ (Shmuel II 2:23), where Rabbi Yochanan said it is the fifth rib, the place where the gall and the liver hang. Some explain וַֽחֲמֻשִּׁים that each of them carried five weapons, and he says the first is right.

וְחִמֵּשׁ אֶת־אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 41:34), that he shall take the fifth of it. On וְאֶת־ חֲמִֽישִׁתוֹ יוֹסֵף עָלָיו (Vayikra 5:16) Chazal explained (Bava Metzia 54a) חומשיה מלבר, that the fifth is reckoned from outside, being a fifth of the principal; and on וַֽחֲמִֽשִׁתָיו יֹסֵף עָלָיו (Vayikra 5:24) they expounded (Bava Kama 108a) that many fifths may come upon one principal. Though by the rule of grammar it should be חֲמִישִׁיּוֹתָיו, in the feminine plural, a masculine plural stands in its place in וַֽאֲחוֹתַיִךְ סְדֹם וּבְנוֹתֶיהָ (Yechezkel 16:55) and נִלְאֵית בְּרֹב עֲצָתָיִךְ (Yeshayahu 47:13); or חמישיתיו is itself in the masculine.

הָאַיִל מְזוּזוֹת חֲמִשִֽׁית (Melachim I 6:31): the doorposts and the lintel were of five sides, one outside the other, each set in from the next, as ornamented doorways are made today. Yonasan rendered it אֵלָהִי וְסִפּוֹהִי מְטַקְסִין, taking the word from וַֽחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ, they went up girded, which is a sense of arraying and ordering.

הרר.sense: A mountain: the full form of the word is הֶרֶר, and the common הַר is that same word with the doubled letter fallen away.

more.t: הֶעֱמַדְתָּה לְֽהַֽרְרִי עֹז (Tehillim 30:8), You set my mountain firm, and בְּהַֽרֲרָם שֵׂעִיר (Bereishis 14:6), in their mountain, Seir; in some sefarim the resh there has a chataf patach and in some a bare sheva. The construct is כְּֽהַרְרֵי ־אֵל (Tehillim 36:7), like the mountains of Kel, and יְסוּדָתוֹ בְּהַרְרֵי ־קֹֽדֶשׁ (Tehillim 87:1), His foundation is in the holy mountains; the adjective is הֲרָרִי בַּשָּׂדֶה (Yirmiyahu 17:3), the one on the mountain in the field. With a heh added, הֶרָה נָּֽסוּ (Bereishis 14:10), they fled to the mountain. The plural is הָרִים, mountains, which would take a dagesh were it not for the resh; and the word is spoken of in the feminine, שְׁמָמָה תִֽהְיֶה הַר ־שֵׂעִיר (Yechezkel 35:15), Har Seir shall be a desolation.
הַרְכֶם צִפּֽוֹר (Tehillim 11:1) he reads as הר שלכם, your mountain; some explain that it is two words instead.

more.h: A form he does not allow
more.t: Some explain בְּהַֽרֲרָם שֵׂעִיר, in their mountain, Seir, as an infinitive of the doubled form. There is an answer against them, from the patach of the heh.

Some take from this הָרוֹת הַגִּלְעָד (Amos 1:13) and וְהָרֹֽתֵיהֶם תְּבַקֵּֽעַ (Melachim II 8:12); if they are of this root and this sense, he means the cities fortified and set high in the mountains. So too הִֽנְנִי אֵלֶיךָ הַר הַמַּשְׁחִית (Yirmiyahu 51:25) is a fortified city, since Bavel is nothing but a plain, and Targum Yonasan rendered it כְּרַכָּא מְחַבְּלָא, the destroying city.

הוד.sense: Splendour and strength: of all its uses together he says ענין כולם הכח וההדר, their sense is power and majesty.

more.t: A string of pesukim and one ruling on them: הוֹד וְהָדָר לָבָֽשְׁתָּ (Tehillim 104:1), You have put on splendour and majesty; הוֹד נַחְרוֹ אֵימָֽה (Iyov 39:20), the majesty of his snorting is a terror; וְלֹא־נָֽתְנוּ עָלָיו הוֹד מַלְכוּת (Daniel 11:21), they did not give him the majesty of kingship; and וְנָֽתַתָּה מֵהֽוֹדְךָ עָלָיו (Bamidbar 27:20), you shall put of your majesty upon him. Rabbi Yonah brought וְלֹא־ הֵד הָרִֽים (Yechezkel 7:7) into this sense too, and he says he has already dealt with that word under the root הָדַד.

ראשׁ.sense: A head; and so the top of a hill, the chief of men, the choicest of spices, the principal of a debt, the sum of a count, and the beginning.

more.t: אֶת־ הָרֹאשׁ (Vayikra 1:8) and רֹאשִׁי רֹאשִׁי (Melachim II 4:19), of which he says only that it is known; and from it יָשׁוּב עֲמָלוֹ בְרֹאשׁוֹ (Tehillim 7:17), his mischief returns on his own head. וַיַּקַּף רֹאשׁ וּתְלָאָֽה (Eichah 3:5) he reads as He compassed my head, and compassed me with weariness; others take the word there as the poison of רֹאשׁ וְלַֽעֲנָֽה (Devarim 29:17). On וְהָיָה לְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִֽׁים (Bereishis 2:10) he says that things divided out of one are called ראשים, each being a head to itself once they have parted, a usage he says is known in other tongues too; Rabbi Yonah made them great rivers, and he holds there is no need for that. כִּי תִשָּׂא אֶת־ רֹאשׁ בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 30:11) is their sum, and וְטִמֵּא רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ (Bamidbar 6:9) the hair of the head of his nezirus.

וַיְהִי דָוִד בָּא עַד־ הָרֹאשׁ (Shmuel II 15:32) is the top of the hill where David used to bow and daven, and Targum Yonasan renders it עַד רֵישׁ טוּרַיָא. They say it is Har HaZeisim, from which he could look at the Beis HaMikdash, and that is why the pasuk says David was going up the ascent of the olives. Though the Beis HaMikdash did not stand then, and its own place was not yet known, Har HaMoriah was known by tradition; which spot on it was not known until Gad told David to build a mizbeach at the threshing floor of Aravnah the Yevusi.

Because the head is the choicest part of the body, the word is used of the pick of men and their chief, and of the best of the spices: בְּשָׂמִים רֹאשׁ (Shemos 30:23), which he reads as take spices, and of them take the chief and choicest. So too רֵאשִׁית שְׁמָנִים יִמְשָׁחוּ (Amos 6:6). On רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק (Bamidbar 24:20) he sends the reader to the Targum; Rabbi Yonah reads it as the greatest and most considerable of them, and by that reading רֵאשִׁית הַחֵרֶם (Shmuel I 15:21) would be the choicest of the spoil.

With the plural suffix the cholam turns to kamatz, רָֽאשֵׁיכֶם שִׁבְטֵיכֶם (Devarim 29:9), and it also comes with the cholam, בְּכָל־ רֹאשָׁיו קָרְחָה (Yeshayahu 15:2). Some books write וַֽחֲבָלִים בְּרֹאשֵׁנוּ (Melachim I 20:31) with the yud of the plural, and the Mesorah there has two, one full and one defective; other books have it defective, and the Mesorah there has two and both defective, counting דָּמוֹ בְרֹאשֵׁנוּ (Yehoshua 2:19), which is how Rabbi Yonah wrote it as well. The alef shows itself in מַרְֽאֲשׁוֹתֵיכֶם (Yirmiyahu 13:18), which he glosses as your greatness; אֲשֶׁר־שָׂם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָיו (Bereishis 28:18) is what he set under his head, and מֵרַֽאֲשֹׁתֵי שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 26:12) is the same without the added mem, that mem being the one that carries the sense of from.

וְשִׁלַּם אֹתוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ (Vayikra 5:24): the principal of a debt is called its ראש, capital in the vernacular, because it is the head and beginning of the thing and the profit comes upon it afterwards. רֹֽאשׁ ־דְּבָרְךָ אֱמֶת (Tehillim 119:160) is the beginning of Your word; רִֽאשֹׁנָה יִסָּֽעוּ (Bamidbar 2:9) is at the first; וַתְּהִי רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בָּבֶל (Bereishis 10:10) is the beginning of his kingdom. בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 1:1), he says, is not in the construct, and reads: at the first Hashem created the heavens and the earth, and after that what came out of them, and only then does the Torah tell that at the beginning of the earth's making it was tohu vavohu.

more.h: First in rank, first in time
more.t: הַיּשְׁבִים רִאשֹׁנָה (Esther 1:14) is first in standing, near the king, and so מִֽיכָאֵל אַחַד הַשָּׂרִים הָֽרִאשֹׁנִים (Daniel 10:13), one of the great in rank. בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ (Yechezkel 29:17) is Nisan, the first of the months, but אַךְ בַּיּוֹם הָֽרִאשׁוֹן תַּשְׁבִּיתוּ שְּׂאֹר (Shemos 12:15) he reads as the day before, the fourteenth, which comes before the seven days of matzah, though he allows the plain reading too, that the leaven be put away on the first day itself. בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ (Yechezkel 40:1) he takes as the seventh month, which is the head of the year, on its tenth, Yom Kippur; Chazal take the tenth day itself to be called Rosh Hashanah and the year to have been a yovel, for which year has its Rosh Hashanah on the tenth if not the yovel. On טוֹב אַֽחֲרִית דָּבָר מֵרֵֽאשִׁיתוֹ (Koheles 7:8) his father explains that the end of a thing is good when a man looks from its beginning to see what its end will be, or else that the good lies in the end, as Chazal say of the man who sees what is to be born.

ארשֹ.sense: He gives no gloss: of אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ and its passive he says only ענינו ידוע, its sense is known.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ (Devarim 20:7), who has betrothed a woman and not taken her; and in the passive, אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ אֹרָשָׂה (Shemos 22:15), who was not betrothed, and הַֽנַּֽעֲרָ הַמְאֹרָשָׂה (Devarim 22:25), the betrothed girl. Of all of them he says only ענינו ידוע.

ארשׁ.sense: The utterance of the lips: one word, אֲרֶשֶׁת, which he glosses מבטא שפתיו.

more.t: One line: וַֽאֲרֶשֶׁת שְׂפָתָיו בַּל־מָנַעְתָּ (Tehillim 21:3), the utterance of his lips You did not withhold, which he glosses מבטא שפתיו, the utterance of his lips.

ציה.sense: Two things under one root: צִי, a ship, and צִיָּה, parched ground and wilderness; and צִיִּים, which are the beasts or the men that dwell there.

more.t: וְצִי אַדִּיר לֹא יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ (Yeshayahu 33:21), no gallant ship shall pass it. In the plural, וְצִים מִיַּד כִּתִּים (Bamidbar 24:24) and יֵֽצְאוּ מַלְאָכִים מִלְּפָנַי בַּצִּים (Yechezkel 30:9), where the root's yud falls away before the yud of the plural; with the yud shown, אַשּׁוּר יְסָדָהּ לְצִיִּים (Yeshayahu 23:13). Their sense, he says, is a ship and ships.

צִיָּה גַם־חֹם (Iyov 24:19), drought and heat, and לַמְרוֹת עֶלְיוֹן בַּצִּיָּֽה (Tehillim 78:17). The feminine plural הָלְכוּ בַּצִּיּוֹת נָהָֽר (Tehillim 105:41) he reads as the water going through the parched place and the wilderness as a river goes. Another pattern is כְּחֹרֶב בְּצָיוֹן (Yeshayahu 25:5), on the weight of רָצוֹן; all of them are drought and wilderness.

וְרָֽבְצוּ־שָׁם צִיִּים (Yeshayahu 13:21) and וּפָֽגְשׁוּ צִיִּים אֶת־אִיִּים (Yeshayahu 34:14) are the beasts that dwell in the ציה, and Targum Yonasan renders them תַּמְוָן. לְפָנָיו יִכְרְעוּ צִיִּים (Tehillim 72:9) he takes as the nations that dwell in the wilderness, or else from the first sense, the men of the ships, since the pasuk goes on to name the kings of Tarshish.

Rabbi Moshe HaKohen takes לְעַם לְצִיִּֽים (Tehillim 74:14) from the ships, its lamed being like the lamed of לְעַבְדְּךָ לְיַֽעֲקֹב (Bereishis 32:19), so that it means the men of the ships. Ibn Ezra reads it of those who dwell in the wilderness: though the creature is in the sea and its strength is great, You give it as food to the dwellers of the desert.

שֹרר.sense: To rule and to be master; and in the reflexive, to set oneself up as a prince over others.

more.t: לִהְיוֹת כָּל־אִישׁ שׂרֵר בְּבֵיתוֹ (Esther 1:22), that every man be master in his own house, and the reflexive כִּֽי־ תִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלֵינוּ גַּם־ הִשְׂתָּרֵֽר (Bamidbar 16:13), that you make yourself a prince over us. He allows that וַיָּשַׂר אֶל־מַלְאָךְ (Hoshea 12:5) and בִּי שָׂרִים יָשׂרוּ (Mishlei 8:16) may belong here, though he filed them under the root שֹוֹר; but וַיָּשַׂר בַּמְּגֵרָה (Divrei HaYamim I 20:3) and אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּל הַמַּשּׂוֹר (Yeshayahu 10:15) he filed under נָשַֹר, which he says is truly their root.

שׁרר.sense: The navel: שָׁרְרֵךְ and שָׁרֵךְ. A second sense is שְׁרִרוּת לֵב, which he glosses as the looking of the heart and its thoughts.

more.t: שָׁרְרֵךְ אַגַּן הַסַּהַר (Shir HaShirim 7:3), your navel a round goblet; לֹֽא־כָרַּת שָׁרֵךְ (Yechezkel 16:4), your navel cord was not cut, where the resh takes a dagesh in place of the doubling that is missing; and in another pattern בִּשְׁרִירֵי בִטְנֽוֹ, of which he says הוא הטבור, it is the navel.

כִּי בִּשְׁרִרוּת לִבִּי אֵלֵךְ (Devarim 29:18), which he glosses ענינו הבטת לבי ומחשבותי, the looking of my heart and my thoughts. With it he sets לְמַעַן שׁוֹרְרָי (Tehillim 5:9) and יָשֹׁר עַל־אֲנָשִׁים (Iyov 33:27), though he notes that he wrote those under the root שׁוּר with nothing to decide between them. Others read בִּשְׁרִרוּת as strength, from Chazal's שריר וקים, valid and standing.

נוף.sense: To drip or sprinkle, and נֹפֶת, flowing honey; to wave a thing back and forth; and נוֹף, a district of the earth.

more.t: נַפְתִּי מִשְׁכָּבִי (Mishlei 7:17), I have sprinkled my bed, which he glosses ענין ההתכה והזלוף בבשמים, melting and sprinkling with spices. The noun is נֹפֶת תִּטֹּפְנָה שִׂפְתוֹתַיִךְ כַּלָּה (Shir HaShirim 4:11), your lips drop honey, and וְנֹפֶת צוּפִֽים (Tehillim 19:11), on the weight of בֹּשֶׁת from בּוּשׁ. Where the verb takes an object, גֶּשֶׁם נְדָבוֹת תָּנִיף אֱלֹהִים (Tehillim 68:10), which he reads as You make it flow down.

הֵנִיף אַֽהֲרֹן תְּנוּפָה (Vayikra 9:21), Aharon waved a wave offering. Chazal explain that he carried it back and forth, and that is what waving is, movement this way and that, while תרומה was lifting up and down: אֲשֶׁר הוּנַף וַֽאֲשֶׁר הוּרָם (Shemos 29:27), what was waved and what was raised.

וְהֵנִיף יָדוֹ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם וְאָסַף הַמְּצֹרָֽע (Melachim II 5:11), he will wave his hand toward the place and gather in the metzora, which he likens to those who whisper over a wound and wave the hand over it this way and that. אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּל הַמַּשּׂוֹר עַל־ מְנִיפוֹ (Yeshayahu 10:15) is said because the saw is waved back and forth by the one who cuts with it. יְנֹפֵף יָדוֹ (Yeshayahu 10:32) he sets beside אַֽחֲרֶיךָ רֹאשׁ הֵנִיעָה (Melachim II 19:21): a man who scorns a thing waves and shakes hand and head at it, and a man calling another waves him over.

more.h: The sieve, and the call to war
more.t: לַֽהֲנָפָה גוֹיִם בְּנָפַת שָׁוְא (Yeshayahu 30:28), to sift the nations in a sieve of vanity; from it the noun נָפָה, which in Chazal's words is the sieve that flour is sifted in, נפה שמוציאה את הקמח וקולטת את הסולת, the sieve that lets out the flour and keeps back the fine meal, so called because it is waved this way and that in the sifting. And הָנִיפוּ יָד וְיָבֹאוּ פִּתְחֵי נְדִיבִֽים (Yeshayahu 13:2), wave the hand and let them come into the gates of the nobles.

יְפֵה נוֹף מְשׂוֹשׂ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (Tehillim 48:3), which he takes as מחוז או פלך, a district or a province; so too כָּל־ נָפַת דֹּאר (Melachim I 4:11) and וּבְנָפוֹת דּוֹר (Yehoshua 11:2), which the Targum renders בְפִלְכֵי דוֹר, and שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַנָּֽפֶת (Yehoshua 17:11), rendered תלתא פלכין.

His father explains that the Creator divided His world into seven parts, the climes, which in lashon hakodesh are נופות. The air of each differs, and a man who leaves the נוף of his birth for another will most often fall ill, the change of air upsetting his own mixture. Yerushalayim was the fairest of the נופות, and whoever came to her from the rest would be sound and whole, and that is מְשׂוֹשׂ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ, the joy of all the earth.

עשֹק.sense: Contention: the well named עֵשֶׂק, and הִתְעַשְּׂקוּ, which he glosses טרידה וערעור, harassing and contesting a claim.

more.t: וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם־הַבְּאֵר עֵשֶׂק (Bereishis 26:20), he called the name of the well Esek, which he notes is written with five points; and from the same root, in the reflexive, כִּי הִֽתְעַשְּׂקוּ עִמּֽוֹ, because they contended with him. Its sense, he says, is טרידה וערעור, harassment and the contesting of a claim, as in Chazal's ויצאו עיליה עשקין, claimants came out against it, that is, one who contests and says it is mine.

עשׁק.sense: To withhold what is another's: money in your hand by deposit, loan or wage owed, which you will not give back. Robbery is taking by force; the two are not one.

more.t: לֹא־ תַֽעֲשֹׁק אֶת־רֵֽעֲךָ וְלֹא תִגְזֹל (Vayikra 19:13) is no doubling, he says: to withhold is where your fellow's money came into your hand as a deposit or a loan, or his wage fell due, and when he asks for it you keep it and say you will not return it; to rob is to snatch it from him or take it by force. So Chazal explained it, bringing וַיִּגְזֹל אֶֽת־הַֽחֲנִית מִיַּד הַמִּצְרִי (Shmuel II 23:21), he wrested the spear out of the Egyptian's hand. The pasuk itself parts the two: אוֹ בְגָזֵל אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת־עֲמִיתֽוֹ (Vayikra 5:21).

וְהַצִּילוּ גָזוּל מִיַּד עָשׁוֹק (Yirmiyahu 22:3), deliver the robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, does not make them one word: a robber certainly withholds too, for once he has taken his fellow's money by force it goes without saying that he keeps it when it is in his hand. עָשׁוֹק itself is an adjective, on the weight of גָּדוֹל, רָחוֹק.

אָדָם עָשֻׁק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁ (Mishlei 28:17): he holds this too is an adjective, the same as עושק for all its shuruk, as his father took שָׁחוּט in Yirmiyahu 9:7 for an adjective like שוחט; the meaning is a man who oppresses others in the blood of a soul, that is, kills men. His father read it the other way, of a man whose yetzer hara oppressed him so that he killed a soul, and until he goes down to Gehinnom no man will hold him up or help him; יָנוּס is said of him because he is in dread all his days.

עָֽשְׁקָה ־לִּי עָרְבֵֽנִי (Yeshayahu 38:14) he takes as a command, though it is not shortened, as שָֽׁמְרָה נַפְשִׁי כִּֽי־חָסִיד אָנִי (Tehillim 86:2) is not; and it asks: be generous and add to my days and my years. He brings Chazal's עשיק לגביך ושוי לכרסיך, be free-handed for your back and buy at value for your belly, that for clothing a man pays above the worth and for his belly pays what the thing is worth. He notes that he had explained the word elsewhere as a past verb in the feminine, my sickness has oppressed me, be my surety, but says that what he has written here is the straight and right reading in his eyes. He reads the pasuk's עֲלֵיהֶם יִֽחְיוּ as the years allotted to a man, on which he may live by Your will as I do, my own allotted days having been completed and fifteen years added to them; and וּלְכָל־בָּהֶן חַיֵּי רוּחִי, that to all men he will tell that in those added years is the life of his spirit.

more.h: By way of figure, and the nouns
more.t: הֵן יַֽעֲשֹׁק נָהָר (Iyov 40:23), which he reads as drawing the whole river into his mouth as though he had taken it by force. In the passive, הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָה בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִידוֹן (Yeshayahu 23:12), the oppressed maiden daughter of Tzidon. The nouns are כִּי הָעֹשֶׁק יְהוֹלֵל חָכָם (Koheles 7:7), oppression makes a wise man mad, and with an added mem, וְרַב מַֽעֲשַׁקּוֹת (Mishlei 28:16) and מֹאֵס בְּבֶצַע מַֽעֲשַׁקּוֹת (Yeshayahu 33:15).

עמד.sense: To stand, and from it to stop, to last and to hold firm; עַמּוּד, a pillar, is what a house stands on; and עִמָּדִי, with me.

more.t: כִּי מִי עָמַד בְּסוֹד (Yirmiyahu 23:18), for who has stood in the counsel of Hashem, and וְאַתָּה פֹּה עֲמֹד עִמָּדִי (Devarim 5:28). עֲמֹד פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל (Shoftim 4:20) is the infinitive, as וְיָֽכָלְתָּ עֲמֹד (Shemos 18:23) is; and וַיָּבֹא אֵצֶל עָמְדִי (Daniel 8:17) is that he came beside me, to the place where I was standing.
וַיַּֽעֲמֹד הַשָּֽׁמֶן (Melachim II 4:6), the oil stopped, no more of it being poured out; and וַֽתַּֽעֲמֹד מִלֶּֽדֶת (Bereishis 29:35), she ceased bearing.

וְיָרֵחַ עָמָד (Yehoshua 10:13) and וַתַּֽעֲמֹד מִלְחָמָה (Divrei HaYamim I 20:4), which he glosses ותתקיים, it held. הֲיַֽעֲמֹד לִבֵּךְ (Yechezkel 22:14), will your heart hold and be strong; וַיַּֽעֲמֹד כָּל־הָעָם בַּבְּרִֽית (Melachim II 23:3), they took strength in accepting the covenant to keep it; לְמַעַן יַֽעַמְדוּ יָמִים רַבִּֽים (Yirmiyahu 32:14), that they last many days; and בֵּין הָעֹֽמְדִים הָאֵֽלֶּה (Zechariah 3:7), among these that endure, which he takes as a hint at the angels, who endure for ever.

עַמּוּדֵי שָׁמַיִם יְרוֹפָפוּ (Iyov 26:11) and וּלְעַמּוּד בַּרְזֶל (Yirmiyahu 1:18) are from this, because the pillars are what keeps the house standing, or what stands beneath it; and by the likeness of a pillar, עַמּוּד הֶֽעָנָן (Shemos 13:22) and וְעַמּוּד הָאֵשׁ.

more.h: Where the verb sets a thing up
more.t: וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵם לָעַד לְעוֹלָם (Tehillim 148:6), He set them to endure for ever; וְהֶֽעֱמַדְנוּ עָלֵינוּ מִצְוֹת (Nechemiah 10:33), we took the mitzvos upon ourselves. On וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ לָהֶם כָּל־מָתְנָֽיִם (Yechezkel 29:7) he says that a man who leans is bent over, and when the prop breaks he straightens up from his bending; Targum Yonasan renders it וְלָא תְהֵי לְהוֹן לְבֵית סוּמְכְוָן, you will not be a house of support to them, that is, you set them on their own loins so that they lean on you no longer, and he notes that he explained the pasuk otherwise under the root מעד. וּמֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה מַֽעֲמִיד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה נֹכַח אֲרָם (Divrei HaYamim II 18:34) is that he held himself up and forced himself, showing himself as though he had not been struck, so that Aram should not take heart against Yisrael in the battle.

לֹא תַֽעֲמֹד עַל־דַּם רֵעֶךָ (Vayikra 19:16) he reads as not holding back from going to save him where you can, as Chazal say: one who sees his fellow drowning in a river, or robbers or a wild beast coming upon him, is bound to save him. יִקַּח מִכֶּם עֶמְדָּתֽוֹ (Michah 1:11) Rabbi Yonah reads as אמדתו, from estimating; he prefers to keep it to standing, that the one will learn his standing from you, since as you did not go out to mourn when your brothers went into exile, so they will not go out while you are in exile. And עִמָּדִי in בְּעוֹד שַׁדַּי עִמָּדִי (Iyov 29:4) is as עִמִּי, with me, perhaps drawn from standing, meaning the place where I stand; he notes that the word is found only with the speaker of the first person.

דוך.sense: To pound in a mortar; pounding is not as fine as grinding, and from this sense the poor man is called דַּךְ.

more.t: אוֹ דָכוּ בַּמְּדֹכָה (Bamidbar 11:8), or they pounded it in a mortar, which he glosses כתשו במכתש. Pounding, he says, is not as fine as grinding, and Chazal parted the two: where the pounding is still wanting all agree the thing is forbidden, and they differ only where the grinding is wanting, from which it appears that grinding is the finer of the two. From this sense the poor man is called דַּךְ, אַל־יָשֹׁב דַּךְ נִכְלָם (Tehillim 74:21), let not the poor turn back ashamed.

אול.sense: A fool, אֱוִיל, which he glosses שוטה; and אִוֶּלֶת, folly, which he holds is a noun and not an adjective.

more.t: אֱוִיל הַנָּבִיא (Hoshea 9:7), the prophet is a fool, and וֶֽאֱוִילִים בַּֽחֲסַר־לֵב יָמֽוּתוּ (Mishlei 10:21), fools die for want of heart; with the yud of relation, כְּלִי רֹעֶה אֱוִלִֽי (Zechariah 11:15). Their sense, he says, is שוטה, שוטים, a fool and fools. On וְאִוֶּלֶת בְּיָדֶיהָ תֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ (Mishlei 14:1) he supplies אשת אולת, a woman of folly, because אִוֶּלֶת is a noun and not an adjective, and so in אִוֶּלֶת אָדָם תְּסַלֵּף דַּרְכּוֹ (Mishlei 19:3). He allows that noun and adjective may share one weight, in which case אִוֶּלֶת בְּיָדֶיהָ would be the adjective, on the pattern of עִוֶּרֶת, the chirik of the one and the patach of the other making no difference to the weight. אוּלַי, he says, he wrote under the root אלה.

ארן.sense: Two words: אֹרֶן, the name of a tree, and אָרוֹן, a chest, which he says is like a תיבה and is used in both genders.

more.t: נָטַע אֹרֶן (Yeshayahu 44:14), he planted an oren, of which he says only that it is the name of a tree, and he brings Chazal's list of woods, עצי ארזים ארנים וברושים, woods of cedar, oren and cypress. Some explain the word as אל צנוב"ר in Arabic.

וְעָשׂוּ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים (Shemos 25:10), they shall make an ark of acacia wood; אֲרוֹן אֶחָד (Melachim II 12:10) he reads as one man's chest; and of וַיִּישֶׂם בָּֽאָרוֹן (Bereishis 50:26) he says only that its sense is known, and that it is like a תיבה. The word is used in both genders, mostly the masculine, and in the feminine at וַֽאֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים נִלְקָֽחָה (Shmuel I 4:17) and אֲשֶׁר־בָּאָה אֲלֵיהֶם אֲרוֹן (Divrei HaYamim II 8:11).

שׁמע.sense: To hear. He parts three: hearing alone, hearing that is acceptance and obedience, and hearing that is understanding.

more.t: All of them are hearing, he says, but some are hearing alone, some שמועה לקבלה, hearing that is acceptance, and some שמועת הבנה, hearing that is understanding: דַּבֶּר־נָא אֶל־עֲבָדֶיךָ אֲרָמִית כִּי שֹֽׁמְעִים אֲנָחְנוּ (Yeshayahu 36:11), speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; גּוֹי אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ תִשְׁמַע לְשֹׁנֽוֹ (Devarim 28:49), a nation whose tongue you will not understand; and לֵב שֹׁמֵעַ (Melachim I 3:9), an understanding heart. He allows that תִּשְׁמַע חֲלוֹם לִפְתֹּר אֹתֽוֹ (Bereishis 41:15) may be of this kind too.

more.h: What the verb takes after it
more.t: It is said with the lamed of a voice, וַיִּשְׁמַע אַבְרָם לְקוֹל שָׂרָֽי (Bereishis 16:2); with the beis, שְׁמַע בְּקֹלִי (Bereishis 27:13) and וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּתֽוֹרָתֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 42:24); with אל, כִּֽי־ שָׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶל־קוֹל הַנַּעַר (Bereishis 21:17); and with על, יַעַן אֲשֶׁר שְׁמַעְתֶּם עַל־מִצְוַת יְהֽוֹנָדָב אֲבִיכֶם (Yirmiyahu 35:18), because you obeyed the command of Yonadav your father, and אַל־ תִּשְׁמְעוּ עַל־דִּבְרֵי הַנְּבִאִים הַנִּבְּאִים לָכֶם (Yirmiyahu 23:16). הִנֵּה שְׁמֹעַ מִזֶּבַח טוֹב (Shmuel I 15:22), to obey is better than a sacrifice.

In the form with tzeirei, אֵת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר שָׁמֵעַ (Yirmiyahu 36:13) and וְשָׂרָה שֹׁמַעַת (Bereishis 18:10); the Nagid wrote that וָֽאֶשְׁמְעָה אֶֽחָד־קָדוֹשׁ (Daniel 8:13) has a kamatz chatuf. The noun כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ שֵׁמַע לְמִצְרָיִם יָחִילוּ כְּשֵׁמַע צֹֽר (Yeshayahu 23:5), as at the report of Mitzrayim so they shall be in pain at the report of Tzor, has tzeirei; some come with segol, as he set out in the part on grammar. In another pattern, שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת־ שָׁמְעוֹ (Yirmiyahu 6:24) and וַיְהִי שָׁמְעוֹ בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ (Yehoshua 6:27), his fame was in all the land; in another, וּבָא בַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה (Yirmiyahu 51:46) and מִי הֶאֱמִין לִשְׁמֻֽעָתֵנוּ (Yeshayahu 53:1); and in another, וְלֹֽא־ לְמִשְׁמַע אָזְנָיו יוֹכִֽיחַ (Yeshayahu 11:3).

וְהַקֹּל נִשְׁמַע (Bereishis 45:16), the report was heard, and וַתִּשָּׁמַע שִׂמְחַת יְרֽוּשָׁלַם מֵרָחֽוֹק (Nechemiah 12:43), the joy of Yerushalayim was heard far off. Of וַיִּשָּׁמַע בְּקוֹלָם (Divrei HaYamim II 30:27) he says their voice was heard for them and found favour. From the same is מִשְׁמַעַת, obedience: וּבְנֵי עַמּוֹן מִשְׁמַעְתָּֽם (Yeshayahu 11:14), which he glosses as their being obedient to them and under their service, and וַיְשִׂמֵהוּ דָוִד אֶל־ מִשְׁמַעְתּֽוֹ (Shmuel II 23:23) and וְסָר אֶל־ מִשְׁמַעְתֶּךָ (Shmuel I 22:14); and לְשֵׁמַֽע אֹזֶן יִשָּׁמְעוּ לִי (Tehillim 18:45).

וַיִּשְׁמַע שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 23:8) he glosses אספם, וקבצם שיהיו נשמעים אליו, he gathered and assembled them that they should be obedient to him; and so הַשְׁמִיעוּ אֶל־בָּבֶל רַבִּים (Yirmiyahu 50:29), gather many against Bavel, that they heed you and come to her, and הַשְׁמִיעוּ עָלֶיהָ מַמְלְכֹות אֲרָרַט מִנִּי וְאַשְׁכְּנָז (Yirmiyahu 51:27). Elsewhere the same form is plain sounding: הִשְׁמִיעַ אֶת־מַֽחֲנֵה אֲרָם (Melachim II 7:6), Hashem made the camp of Aram hear, and הַשְׁמִיעוּ הַֽלְלוּ וְאִמְרוּ (Yirmiyahu 31:6).

וְאָסָף בַּֽמְצִלְתַּיִם מַשְׁמִֽיעַ (Divrei HaYamim I 15:5), Asaf sounding the cymbals, which he glosses משמיע קול, making a sound to be heard; and וְעִמָּהֶם הֵימָן וִֽידוּתוּן חֲצֹֽצְרוֹת וּמְצִלְתַּיִם לְמַשְׁמִיעִים (Divrei HaYamim I 16:42), where the lamed is to be sounding, as in וְחֶרֶב אֽוֹיְבֶיךָ לְמַשֶּׂגֶת (Divrei HaYamim I 21:12) it is to be overtaking. The noun לְהַשְׁמָעוּת אָזְנָֽיִם (Yechezkel 24:26) is from the same.

שׁכן.sense: To dwell, and to settle a thing in a place; שָׁכֵן, a neighbour, and מִשְׁכָּן, a dwelling. Said of the mighty, it is the rest of death.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר שָֽׁכַן ־שָׁם (Yehoshua 22:19), where He dwelt; וְשָֽׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָֽם (Shemos 25:8), I shall dwell among them; שְׁכֹן בָּאָרֶץ (Bereishis 26:2), dwell in the land; and לִשְׁכֹּן בָּֽעֲרָפֶֽל (Melachim I 8:12), to dwell in the thick darkness. לְשִׁכְנוֹ תִדְרְשׁוּ (Devarim 12:5) has a chirik, and he takes it for an infinitive on the weight of וּכְפִתְחוֹ עָֽמְדוּ כָל־הָעָֽם (Nechemiah 8:5), or else for a noun.

מִשְׁכַּן (Vayikra 17:4), the Mishkan of Hashem; מִשְׁכָּנוֹת לַֽאֲבִיר יַֽעֲקֹֽב (Tehillim 132:5), dwellings for the Mighty One of Yaakov; and וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָיו מְלֵֽחָה (Iyov 39:6), his dwellings the salt land. The masculine plural is in קְדשׁ מִשְׁכְּנֵי עֶלְיֽוֹן (Tehillim 46:5).

וּשְׁכֵנוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ (Shemos 12:4), his neighbour nearest his house; the feminine וְשָֽׁאֲלָה אִשָּׁה מִשְּׁכֶנְתָּהּ (Shemos 3:22), and the plural וַתִּקְרֶאנָה לוֹ הַשְּׁכֵנוֹת (Rus 4:17). A שכן, he says, is one who dwells beside a man, his house beside his house; but וּבַל־יֹאמַר שָׁכֵן חָלִיתִי (Yeshayahu 33:24) is of one who dwells inside her, in Yerushalayim, as the pasuk goes on, הָעָם הַיּשֵׁב בָּהּ נְשֻׂא עָוֹֽן, the people that dwell in her are forgiven their sin; and יָגוּרוּ שְׁכַן שֹֽׁמְרוֹן (Hoshea 10:5) is those who dwell in Shomron.

more.h: Settling a thing, and the rest of death
more.t: Where the verb takes an object, אֹהֶל שִׁכֵּן בָּאָדָֽם (Tehillim 78:60), the tent He set to dwell among men, and לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם (Devarim 12:11), to set His name to dwell there; וְהִשְׁכַּנְתִּי עָלֶיךָ כָּל־עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (Yechezkel 32:4), I will settle all the birds of the sky upon you, and וּכְבוֹדִי לֶֽעָפָר יַשְׁכֵּן סֶֽלָה (Tehillim 7:6). From this sense he derives יִשְׁכְּנוּ אַדִּירֶיךָ (Nachum 3:18), which he says is the rest of death, and with it שָֽׁכְנָה דוּמָה נַפְשִֽׁי (Tehillim 94:17), my soul dwelt in silence.

שֹכן.sense: One pasuk, וְשַׂמְתָּ שַׂכִּין בְּלֹעֶךָ (Mishlei 23:2), of which he says only ידוע, its sense is known.

more.t: Two lines: וְשַׂמְתָּ שַׂכִּין בְּלֹעֶךָ (Mishlei 23:2), and you shall put a knife to your throat, of which he says only ידוע, it is known; and that he has already written the word in another sense under the root שֹוֹך, with לְשִׂכִּים בְּעֵינֵיכֶם (Bamidbar 33:55).

נבל.sense: All of it is falling: a leaf that withers, a man who is base, a vile deed, the carcass that falls; and, apart, נֵבֶל, a jar and a musical instrument.

more.t: נָבֵֽל צִיץ (Yeshayahu 40:7), the blossom withers, formed like יָבֵשׁ חָצִיר, the grass dries, in that same pasuk; כִּנְבֹל עָלֶה מִגֶּפֶן (Yeshayahu 34:4), as a leaf withers from the vine; and the adjective וְהֶֽעָלֶה נָבֵל (Yirmiyahu 8:13), the withered leaf. וַנָּבֶל כֶּֽעָלֶה כֻּלָּנוּ (Yeshayahu 64:5), we all wither like a leaf, carries a kamatz where a dagesh would stand, as וַיָּזֶד יַֽעֲקֹב נָזִיד (Bereishis 25:29) does; or it is a passive form. All of them, he says, are a sense of נפילה, falling.

כְּאֵלָה נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), a terebinth whose leaf withers: the tree is called withering from the side of its leaves, not of itself. So too מְגֻלְּחֵי זָקָן (Yirmiyahu 41:5), men whose beard is shaven, and וּקְרֻעֵי בְגָדִים, whose clothes are torn; חָגוּר כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָֽה (Shoftim 18:11), whose loins are girded with weapons of war; and הָעִיר הַיֹּצֵאת אֶלֶף (Amos 5:3), the city that goes out a thousand, since it is the men of the city who go out.

A low and fallen man is called נבל: כִּי נָבָל נְבָלָה יְדַבֵּר (Yeshayahu 32:6), a base man speaks baseness, and כְּאַחַד הַנְּבָלִים (Shmuel II 13:13), like one of the base. אִם־ נָבַלְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂא (Mishlei 30:32) he reads as counsel to one brought down: if you have fallen from your greatness, bear yourself with honour, and do not ask of base men or of men unworthy of your asking; hold yourself as dear as you were before, and refrain from what disgraces you. That is וְאִם־זַמּוֹתָ יָד לְפֶה, and if you thought to ask, set a hand to the mouth.

Where the verb takes an object it lowers: אַל־ תְּנַבֵּל כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ (Yirmiyahu 14:21), do not bring down the throne of Your glory, and וַיְנַבֵּל צוּר יְשֻֽׁעָתֽוֹ (Devarim 32:15), he brought down the Rock of his salvation from its greatness in his thought and by his deeds. וְנִבַּלְתִּיךְ (Nachum 3:6) is either I will make you foul and disgraced or I will make you like a carcass thrown out; and נְבָלָה (Iyov 42:8) is a foul and disgraceful thing, as בְּנִבְלַת שִׁקּֽוּצֵיהֶם (Yirmiyahu 16:18) is the foulness of their idols. The dead body is called נְבֵלָה because it falls, וְחֵלֶב נְבֵלָה (Vayikra 7:24), the fat of a carcass; and that a dead body is spoken of as a falling is plain from מַפֶּלֶת הָאַרְיֵה (Shoftim 14:8), the fallen lion.

נֵבֶל יִמָּלֵא יָיִן (Yirmiyahu 13:12), a נֵבֶל filled with wine, is a leather skin or a potter's vessel, as כְּשֵׁבֶר נֵבֶל יֽוֹצְרִים (Yeshayahu 30:14), the breaking of a potter's vessel. The other is the instrument of music, בְּנֵבֶל וְכִנּֽוֹר (Tehillim 150:3), with nevel and kinnor; on בִכְלִי־ נֶבֶל (Tehillim 71:22) the Mesorah marks it the one place pointed so. Targum Yonasan renders מִכְּלֵי הָֽאַגָּנוֹת וְעַד כָּל־כְּלֵי הַנְּבָלִֽים (Yeshayahu 22:24) as from the kohanim who wear the ephod to the Levi'im who hold the nevalim.
וְנִבְלֵי שָׁמַיִם מִי יַשְׁכִּֽיב he glosses as the rains of heaven; and from the same he takes וַיְהִי הַמַּבּוּל (Bereishis 7:17), the flood, whose rule is מַנְבּוּל.

יקץ.sense: Of the sense he says only that it is known; the pesukim he brings are Yaakov awaking from his sleep and Noach from his wine.

more.t: Three pesukim and a note on the pointing: וַיִּיקַץ יַֽעֲקֹב מִשְּׁנָתוֹ (Bereishis 28:16), Yaakov awoke from his sleep; וַיִּיקֶץ נֹחַ מִיֵּינוֹ (Bereishis 9:24), Noach awoke from his wine; and וְיִֽקְצוּ מְזַעְזְעֶיךָ (Chavakuk 2:7), those who shake you will awake, where the yud is held by a ga'ya because the yud that is the first root letter has dropped.

כחל.sense: To paint the eyes with kohl, which is the פּוּךְ.

more.t: One line, on כָּחַלְתְּ עֵינַיִךְ (Yechezkel 23:40), you painted your eyes: he glosses it as setting your eyes off with the kohl that is the פּוּךְ, and says the Arabic name for it is al-kuhl.

גבל.sense: A border; the verb is a thing bordering on another, and where it takes an object, setting a bound, as the people and the mountain are bounded off.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר גָּֽבְלוּ רִֽאשֹׁנִים (Devarim 19:14), which earlier men set as a border; וְהַיַּרְדֵּן יִגְבֹּֽל ־אֹתוֹ (Yehoshua 18:20), the Yarden borders it; and וְגַם־חֲמָת תִּגְבָּל ־בָּהּ (Zecharya 9:2), which he glosses as Chamas being a border to her. Where it takes an object, וְהִגְבַּלְתָּ אֶת־הָעָם (Shemos 19:12) and הַגְבֵּל אֶת־הָהָר (Shemos 19:23), to set a bound.

מִגְבָּלֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם (Shemos 28:14), bordered work, formed like וְהֶֽעָרִים הַמִּבְדָּלוֹת (Yehoshua 16:9), the cities set apart; the feminine וְכֻסֶּמֶת גְּבֻלָתֽוֹ, spelt in its border, with the plural גְּבֻלוֹת יַשִּׂיגוּ (Iyov 24:2), they move borders; and in another pattern שַֽׁרְשֹׁת גַּבְלֻת (Shemos 28:22), chains of border work, formed like עַבְדּוּת, servitude.

הַגִּבְלִים (Melachim I 5:30) he takes as the men who cut the stone by line and measure, as the corners of a house are cut by line and measure, setting a red thread at the end of their measure or ruling a line and cutting the stone from there: a bound set to the stone's measure. Others explained גִּבְלִים as the men of Geval, who were craftsmen in stone, as זִקְנֵי גְבַל וַֽחֲכָמֶיהָ (Yechezkel 27:9).

גרם.sense: A bone, which is how the Targum renders עֶצֶם, bone; and the verb is breaking the bones, or leaving none of them.

more.t: יִשָּׂשכָר חֲמֹר גָּרֶם (Bereishis 49:14) he takes as strong and big of bone, bearing a great load, which is why the pasuk goes on וַיֵּט שִׁכְמוֹ לִסְבֹּל, he bent his shoulder to bear. Rabbi Yonah takes it as broken and unable to stir from his place, from וְעַצְמֹֽתֵיהֶם יְגָרֵם (Bamidbar 24:8).

וְעַצְמֹֽתֵיהֶם יְגָרֵם is he will break the bones, formed as יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ (Iyov 31:8) is he will take away the roots. לֹא גָֽרְמוּ לַבֹּֽקֶר (Tzefaniah 3:3) is either that they did not tear prey, since a lion or a wolf in tearing breaks the bones by morning, or that they left not even the bones for morning; and by way of figure, וְאֶת־חֲרָשֶׂיהָ תְּגָרֵמִי (Yechezkel 23:34), you will gnaw its shards.

אֶל־ גֶּרֶם הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Melachim II 9:13) is the steps themselves, or else a step in the sense of a degree. Yonasan renders it שַׁעֲיָא, the step that carried a mark for the hours of the day, as he renders צֵל הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Yeshayahu 38:8), the shadow of the steps, טוּל אֶבֶן שְׁעַיָא.

גמל.sense: To deal out good or ill and so to repay; to wean a child, and of fruit to come ripe; and the camel, of which he says only that it is known.

more.t: He calls it the beginning of the good or the evil rather than the return of it: כִּי גָמַל עָלָֽי (Tehillim 13:6), He dealt with me; אֲשֶׁר־ גְּמָלָם כְּֽרַֽחֲמָיו (Yeshayahu 63:7), as He dealt with them according to His mercies; and אֲשֶׁר גָּמַלְנוּ אֹתֽוֹ (Bereishis 50:15), all that we dealt him.

הַגְּמוּל אַתֶּם מְשַׁלְּמִים (Yoel 4:4), is it a recompense you are paying; with the feminine ending, הַגְּמוּלָה הַזֹּֽאת (Shmuel II 19:37), this recompense; and in another pattern כָּֽל־ תַּגְמוּלוֹהִי עָלָֽי (Tehillim 116:12), all He has dealt to me, which stands for תַּגְמוּלָיו and takes its ending in the Aramaic way, as עֲלוֹהִי and יְדוֹהִי do.

וַיִּגְדַּל הַיֶּלֶד וַיִּגָּמַל (Bereishis 21:8), the child grew and was weaned, which he glosses as his nursing being completed, and עַד יִגָּמֵל הַנַּעַר (Shmuel I 1:22), until the boy is weaned; so גְּמוּלֵי מֵֽחָלָב, those weaned from milk. The ripening of fruit is the same completing: וַיִּגְמֹל שְׁקֵדִֽים (Bamidbar 17:23), it ripened almonds, and וּבֹסֶר גֹּמֵל (Yeshayahu 18:5), the sour grape ripening.

אֶת־ הַגָּמָל כִּי־מַֽעֲלֵה גֵרָה הוּא (Vayikra 11:4), the camel, for it brings up the cud, and גְּמַלִּים מֵֽינִיקוֹת (Bereishis 32:16), nursing camels. Of the animal itself he says only that it is known.

שׁוב.sense: Three senses: turning back, and so turning from sin; שָׁב שְׁבוּת, returning a captivity, which is quieting and rest; and מְשׁוּבָה, backsliding, rebellion.

more.t: וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לֽוֹ he glosses as turning back from his sin, and so וּלְשָׁבֵי פֶשַׁע בְּיַֽעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 59:20), those who turn from transgression in Yaakov, and כִּֽי־אַֽחֲרֵי שׁוּבִי נִחַמְתִּי (Yirmiyahu 31:19), after I had turned back from my sins I was sorry. A city returns in the same way: at Yechezkel 35:9 your cities will not return, that is, not return to what they were.

more.h: The rain that does not return
more.t: וְשָׁמָּה לֹא יָשׁוּב כִּי אִם־הִרְוָה אֶת־הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 55:10) he reads with כִּי אִם for but rather: it does not go back there, and what does it do? It waters the earth. His father reads it as it stands, that it does not return until it has watered but returns once it has, which is the going up of the rain, since the heat of the sun draws it; and were that not so, the earth would have no need of rain.

Where the verb takes an object it gives back: וַיָּשֶׁב אֵת כָּל־הָֽרְכֻשׁ (Bereishis 14:16), he brought back all the goods, and וַיָּשִׁיבוּ אֹתָם דָּבָר (Bamidbar 13:26), they brought them back word; reaching a third, לָכֵן שְׂעִפַּי יְשִׁיבוּנִי (Iyov 20:2), my thoughts force me to return you an answer. A מִנְחָה is called a returning because it repays a good done, or repays the man feared for not harming; an אָשָׁם, because the sinner who brings it is a debtor returning his debt to its owner. What seems right to him further is that a מִנְחָה is a returning because it comes time after time, as וְהֵשִׁיב לְמֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim II 3:4), which was done year by year.

נַפְשִׁי יְשׁוֹבֵב (Tehillim 23:3), He restores my soul, is bringing it back to the good way, and מְשׁוֹבֶבֶת מֵחֶרֶב (Yechezkel 38:8) is a land whose people escaped the sword of the nations and came back to her. On לְשׁוֹבֵב שָׂדֵינוּ יְחַלֵּֽק (Michah 2:4) he reads: while we look for our fields to be given back to us, they divide them among themselves. וְלִתְשׁוּבַת הַשָּׁנָה (Divrei HaYamim II 36:10) is the year's end, when the sun comes back to the point it set out from.

more.h: Returning a captivity, and a dispute
more.t: At Devarim 30:3, where He brings back אֶת־שְׁבֽוּתְךָ, your captivity, and at הִֽנְנִי־ שָׁב שְׁבוּת (Yirmiyahu 30:18), behold I bring back a captivity, the sense is quieting and rest, as Rabbi Yehudah wrote. Rabbi Yonah objected: what sense is there in quieting them in exile? That is no sound argument, he answers, for the navi says He will quiet the exile and give them rest from their trouble, and that cannot be except by returning them to their place, since a man exiled from his land has no quiet even among great delights; and Rabbi Yehudah is right that the whole light verb in the first sense stands of itself and takes no object. שׁוּבָה (Bamidbar 10:36) he sets in this second sense, while his father sets it in the first, as the Targum has תּוּב, return: through the three days the Aron went before them Moshe said קוּמָה and וְיָפֻצוּ אֹֽיְבֶיךָ (Bamidbar 10:35), let Your enemies scatter, and when it came back to its place inside the camp, where it always travelled, he said רִֽבֲבוֹת אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel: return and go with them as at first.

The third sense is rebellion: מְשֻֽׁבוֹתַיִךְ תּֽוֹכִחֻךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:19), your backslidings will reprove you; כִּי מְשׁוּבַת פְּתָיִם תַּֽהַרְגֵם (Mishlei 1:32), the backsliding of the simple kills them; מְשֻׁבָה נִצַּחַת (Yirmiyahu 8:5), an unbroken backsliding; and the adjective שׁוּבָה מְשֻׁבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yirmiyahu 3:12), return, backsliding Israel, with שׁוּבוּ בָנִים שֽׁוֹבָבִים (Yirmiyahu 3:14), return, backsliding children. וְעַמִּי תְלוּאִים לִמְשֽׁוּבָתִי he reads as: for the backsliding they work toward Me they hang in their trouble, not knowing where to turn for help.

שֹוב.sense: To grow grey; and שֵׂיבָה, grey hair, which is further on in a man's years than old age.

more.t: זָקַנְתִּי וָשַׂבְתִּי (Shmuel I 12:2), I have grown old and grey; the adjective גַּם־ שָׂב גַּם־יָשִׁישׁ בָּנוּ, both the grey and the aged are among us; the noun כִּי קָמוּ עֵינָיו מִשֵּׂיבֽוֹ (Melachim I 14:4), his eyes were set through his age; and with the feminine ending גַּם־ שֵׂיבָה זָרְקָה בּוֹ (Hoshea 7:9), grey hairs are sprinkled on him. Grey hair is further on than זקנה, old age, as the Mishnah in Avos has it, sixty for old age and seventy for grey hair, and so the pasuk means: I grew grey after I had grown old.

חפה.sense: To cover, and to overlay a thing with gold or with wood; and, with an alef for the last root letter, to cover one's deeds over from the Creator.

more.t: וּפְנֵי הָמָן חָפֽוּ (Esther 7:8) he takes as a verb standing of itself: his face was pressed down to the ground, for he was ashamed at what the king said to him. Others take it as a verb with an object like its fellows, that the king's servants covered his face as the faces of those to be hanged are covered, since they saw how angry the king was and understood that he would order him hanged; and so Charvonah said גַּם הִנֵּה־הָעֵץ (Esther 7:9), here too is the tree.

חִפָּה עֵץ בְּרוֹשִׁים (Divrei HaYamim II 3:5), he overlaid it with cypress wood, and וַיְחַפֵּהוּ זָהָב טוֹב, and overlaid it with fine gold; in the passive, כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה נֶחְפָּה בַכֶּסֶף (Tehillim 68:14), a dove's wings covered with silver. All of it is covering, and the Targum of וַיְכַס (Shemos 10:15), and it covered, is וַחֲפָא.

וַיְחַפְּאוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim II 17:9), where an alef stands for the last root letter: they drew a screen between themselves and the Creator, saying that the deeds of men are hidden from Him and that He neither knows nor grasps anything of them, and therefore built themselves high places, the whole parsha running so. Yeshayahu says the like of them, woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel, whose deeds are in the dark, who say who sees us and who knows us (Yeshayahu 29:15), and the navi says they say He does not see us and has forsaken the land (Yechezkel 8:12). Chazal explained it in the Yalkut: what did they say? This pillar neither sees nor hears.

קסס.sense: To be plucked off; he glosses it as קטף, plucking, and takes it as יְקוֹצֵץ with a tzadi, cutting off.

more.t: One line, on יְקוֹסֵס וְיָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:9), it will be plucked off and wither.

אתה.sense: To come. All of them together, he says, are a sense of coming, as the Targum of ויבא, and he came, is ואתא.

more.t: אָתָא בֹקֶר וְגַם־לָיְלָה (Yeshayahu 21:12), morning comes and night too, and עָדֶיךָ תֵאתֶה (Michah 4:8), it will come to you, have the alef at rest; מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶֽאֱתֶה (Iyov 37:22), gold comes out of the north, and כְּסוּפָה יֶֽאֱתֶה (Mishlei 1:27), it comes like a storm, have it sounded. In הַעִירוֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן וַיַּאת (Yeshayahu 41:25), I roused one from the north and he came, the last root letter has dropped; and in וַיֵּתֶא רָאשֵׁי עָם (Devarim 33:21), he came with the heads of the people, the alef stands for the heh that is the last root letter.

הָאֹֽתִיּוֹת שְׁאָלוּנִי (Yeshayahu 45:11), ask Me of the things to come, and הַגִּידוּ הָאֹֽתִיּוֹת לְאָחוֹר (Yeshayahu 41:23), tell what is to come hereafter. In these the last root letter shows itself turned into a yud, as it does in קָֽרְבוּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן (Yeshayahu 41:5), they drew near and came, and in כִּי פַחַד פָּחַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵנִי (Iyov 3:24), what I feared has come upon me.

more.h: Come, with a heh for the alef
more.t: אֵתָיוּ אֶקְחָה־יַיִן (Yeshayahu 56:12), come, let me fetch wine; and with a heh in place of the alef that is the first root letter, הֵתָיוּ לְאָכְלָֽה (Yirmiyahu 12:9), come to devour, and לִקְרַאת צָמֵא הֵתָיוּ מָיִם (Yeshayahu 21:14), which he reads as telling the waters to come toward the thirsty man, the one wandering from his place before the sword.

תמם.sense: To come to an end and be used up; and, in a sense he calls close to it, to be whole in body with no limb lacking, or whole in mind and in good traits.

more.t: כִּי אִם ־תַּם הַכֶּסֶף (Bereishis 47:18), when the money was spent, and וַתִּתֹּם הַשָּׁנָה (Bereishis 47:18), the year ended; לֹֽא־יִבּוֹל עָלֵהוּ וְלֹֽא־ יִתֹּם פִּרְיוֹ (Yechezkel 47:12), its leaf will not wither and its fruit will not fail; עַד־ תֹּם כָּל־הַדּוֹר (Devarim 2:14), till the whole generation was gone. Where it takes an object, עַד־ תֻּמִּי אֹתָם בְּיָדֽוֹ (Yirmiyahu 27:8), until I make an end of them by his hand. כְּתֻמָּם בָּאוּ עָלַיִךְ (Yeshayahu 47:9) is at their completion: bereavement and widowhood came upon you entire, all the evil that could come of them.

תַּמְנוּ חֵפֶשׂ מְחֻפָּשׂ (Tehillim 64:7): the nun stands in place of the doubled letter, the rule being תממו, and the sense is that they search out wrongs until they are finished, so that no man could think out or search out more wrong than they search. So too כִּי לֹא־ תָמְנוּ (Eichah 3:22), which is either that the kindnesses are not spent or that we ourselves are not spent; and like it הַאִם תַּמְנוּ לִגְוֹֽעַ (Bamidbar 17:28), have we done with dying.

תָּמִים הָיָה בְּדֹֽרֹתָיו (Bereishis 6:9), whole in his generations; זָכָר תָּמִים (Vayikra 1:3), an unblemished male; יוֹנָתִי תַמָּתִי (Shir HaShirim 5:2), my dove, my perfect one; תֹּם ־וָישֶׁר (Tehillim 25:21), wholeness and uprightness; and וְאִישׁ מָשַׁךְ בַּקֶּשֶׁת לְתֻמּוֹ (Melachim I 22:34), a man drew the bow in his innocence, meaning that he did not aim at Achav. On פַּר בֶּן־בָּקָר תְּמִימִם (Yechezkel 46:6) he reads the plural as meaning that bull and herd beast alike be unblemished, and brings Chazal (Menachos 45a): since the parsha elsewhere says two bulls for the new moon, פַּר in the singular teaches that one who found only one brings one, and the plural תְּמִימִם stands because the obligation is two. From this root and sense he takes אֶת־הָֽאוּרִים וְאֶת־ הַתֻּמִּים (Shemos 28:30).

more.h: The day that did not hasten
more.t: וְלֹֽא־אָץ לָבוֹא כְּיוֹם תָּמִֽים (Yehoshua 10:13): the sun stood still for Yehoshua and did not hurry to set, and the day was like the full day of the year, the day of the turn of Tammuz.

אֵֽין־ מְתֹם בִּבְשָׂרִי (Tehillim 38:4), no soundness in my flesh, since all of it is stricken; and in אֵין־בּוֹ מְתֹם (Yeshayahu 1:6) the word רק, but, is left out: there is nothing sound in it but wound and bruise. So too אֵֽין־טוֹב בָּֽאָדָם שֶׁיֹּאכַל וְשָׁתָה (Koheles 2:24), nothing good in a man but that he eat and drink.

His father writes that every form doubled in the tav alone belongs to a root נָתַם, all of them a sense of consuming and completing. Yonasan renders וְכֵן הֵתַֽמוּ (Shmuel II 20:18) as אִם מַשְׁלְמִין, whether you will make peace: the asking should have been made at Avel first, as כִּֽי־תִקְרַב אֶל־עִיר (Devarim 20:10) requires, and all the more so for a city of Israel, which is why she said after it אנכי שלומי אמוני ישראל, I am of the peaceable and faithful of Israel.

רצה.sense: To be pleased with a thing and take it as acceptable; to pay off in full, as the land pays off her sabbaths; and, in a third sense, to run.

more.t: כִּֽי־ רָצוּ עֲבָדֶיךָ אֶת־אֲבָנֶיהָ (Tehillim 102:15), Your servants take pleasure in her stones; וְאֶרְצֶה ־בּוֹ (Chaggai 1:8), I shall be pleased with it; וְכִי יַֽעֲלוּ עֹלָה וּמִנְחָה אֵינֶנִּי רֹצָם (Yirmiyahu 14:12), though they bring up an olah and a minchah I do not accept them; and the one accepted, יְהִי רְצוּי אֶחָיו (Devarim 33:24), let him be acceptable to his brothers. Where the verb takes an object, בָּנָיו יְרַצּוּ דַלִּים (Iyov 20:10), his sons will appease the poor, and one makes himself acceptable, וּבַמֶּה יִתְרַצֶּה זֶה אֶל־אֲדֹנָיו (Shmuel I 29:4). The noun is וַיָּפֶק רָצוֹן (Mishlei 8:35), he draws out favour, and וּבִרְצֹנָם עִקְּרוּ־שֽׁוֹר (Bereishis 49:6), in their will they hamstrung an ox.

אִם־תִּֽהְיֶה לְטוֹב לְהָעָם הַזֶּה וּרְצִיתָם (Divrei HaYamim II 10:7) he takes as their being made acceptable, while Rabbi Yonah takes the verb as reaching an object, that you will win them over with your good words.

more.h: What the olah makes acceptance for
more.t: On וְנִרְצָה לוֹ (Vayikra 1:4) he brings Chazal in the Sifra: not for kareisos, nor for the deaths at the hands of beis din or of heaven, nor for lashes, since the punishment of those is stated; only for a positive commandment, and for a negative that a positive puts right, whose punishment is not stated. A man who brings an olah as a gift, though he was not commanded in it, has it accepted for him to atone for what he sinned in these.

A second sense: עַד־ רָֽצְתָה הָאָרֶץ אֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתֶיהָ (Divrei HaYamim II 36:21), until the land had paid off her sabbaths; אָז תִּרְצֶה הָאָרֶץ (Vayikra 26:34), then the land will pay off; וְהֵם יִרְצוּ אֶת־עֲוֹנָם (Vayikra 26:41), they will pay off their sin; עַד־ יִרְצֶה כְּשָׂכִיר יוֹמֽוֹ (Iyov 14:6), till he has out his day like a hired man; and in the passive כִּי נִרְצָה עֲוֹנָהּ (Yeshayahu 40:2), her sin is paid off. He calls it a sense of completing, close to the first.

A third sense: אִם־רָאִיתָ גַנָּב וַתִּרֶץ עִמּוֹ (Tehillim 50:18), if you saw a thief you ran with him, whose rule is וַתִּרְצֶה, and וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב (Yechezkel 1:14), the chayos running out and back, where an alef stands for a heh. Rabbi Yonah takes בִּרְצֹתוֹ עִם־אֱלֹהִֽים (Iyov 34:9) here too, as his walking with Hashem, but there is no need, he holds, to take it from its plain sense. One may read ותרץ עמו itself from willing, that you wished to be with him, and others read וּרְצִיתָם so as well, that you go along with them after their own mind and wish.

וְאַֽחֲרֵיהֶם בְּפִיהֶם יִרְצוּ סֶֽלָה (Tehillim 49:14): those after them are their sons, and the sons of the wicked are pleased with what their father charged them concerning the oppression and the violence, which is בְּפִיהֶם, by what they say to them and charge them. Others read it from going: they go after them to death in their going, and בְּפִיהֶם stands for כְּפִיהֶם, after their manner, as אִישׁ כְּפִי עֲבֹֽדָתֽוֹ (Bamidbar 7:5) and לְפִי אָכְלוֹ (Shemos 12:4) mean like.

שׁמם.sense: To lie waste, and to be appalled; all of it, he ends, is one sense of שממה, desolation, part of it ruin and part of it astonishment.

more.h: The two sides of the one sense
more.t: Ruin: עַל הַר־צִיּוֹן שֶׁשָּׁמֵם (Eichah 5:18), Har Tzion that lies waste, and שְׁמָמָה תִֽהְיֶה כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (Yirmiyahu 4:27), the whole land will be a waste. Astonishment: כַּֽאֲשֶׁר שָֽׁמְמוּ עָלֶיךָ רַבִּים (Yeshayahu 52:14), as many were appalled at you; יָשֹׁמּוּ יְשָׁרִים עַל־זֹאת (Iyov 17:8), the upright are appalled at this; שֹׁמּוּ שָׁמַיִם (Yirmiyahu 2:12), be appalled, heavens; and וָאֵֽשְׁבָה מְשׁוֹמֵֽם (Ezra 9:3), I sat appalled.

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: אֶשֹּׁם וְאֶשְׁאַף (Yeshayahu 42:14) takes an object, he says, in his own view, and so שַׁמּוֹת וְשָׁאֹף אֶתְכֶם מִסָּבִיב (Yechezkel 36:3), laying you waste and swallowing you from every side. מַשְׁמִים בְּתוֹכָֽם (Yechezkel 3:15), sitting appalled among them, stands of itself; and וְעַל כְּנַף שִׁקּוּצִים מְשֹׁמֵם, on a wing of abominations one that appalls, is either appalling those who see it or itself standing of itself, that at the spreading of the abominations a man is appalled and astonished.

שִֽׁמְמוֹת עוֹלָם אֶתֶּנְךָ (Yechezkel 35:9), I will make you everlasting desolations; מְשַׁמָּה, and כִּֽי־מֵי נִמְרִים מְשַׁמּוֹת יִֽהְיוּ (Yeshayahu 15:6), the waters of Nimrim will be wastes; בִּמְשׂוּרָה וּבְשִׁמָּמוֹן יִשְׁתּֽוּ (Yechezkel 4:16), they will drink by measure and in dismay; and שַׁמָּה וְשַֽׁעֲרוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 5:30), an appalling and horrible thing.

more.h: A command, and how to point it
more.t: פְּנֽוּ־אֵלַי וְהָשַׁמּוּ (Iyov 21:5), turn to me and be appalled: he has the shin without a dagesh and the heh under a full kamatz, as the accurate books have it, a command whose pasach under the shin stands for a tzere, its rule being וְהָשֵׁמּוּ. Rabbi Yonah has the shin with a dagesh and the heh then read with a chataf kamatz; he too takes it as a command, and says it should have gone like הָסֵבִּי עֵינַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 6:5), turn your eyes away.
אִם־לֹא יַשִּׁים עֲלֵיהֶם נְוֵהֶֽם (Yirmiyahu 49:20), will he not make their fold desolate over them, he brings here, but his father writes that ישים has its own root, יָשַׁם.

כִּֽי־רַבִּים בְּֽנֵי־ שׁוֹמֵמָה (Yeshayahu 54:1), the children of the desolate one are many, where she is a woman with no husband. Of a man, שָׂמַנִי שֹׁמֵֽם (Eichah 3:11), He made me desolate, and הָיוּ בָנַי שֽׁוֹמֵמִים (Eichah 1:15), my children are desolate, which appears with a nun for a mem at כָּל־שְׁעָרֶיהָ שֽׁוֹמֵמִין (Eichah 1:4), all her gates are desolate.

שֹמם.sense: The שְׂמָמִית of Mishlei, which he does not settle: the swallow, or a creature kept in palaces for sport, or the spider.

more.t: שְׂמָמִית בְּיָדַיִם תְּתַפֵּשׂ (Mishlei 30:28), the semamis takes hold with her hands. Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is the katuf in Arabic, which is הדרור, the swallow, called in la'az arondela. Others say it is the one called bugia in la'az, whose shape is a man's shape, which catches in its hands whatever is given it and is kept in the palaces of kings to play with. And it may be the arania of la'az, the one that builds her house even in the palaces of a king.

Chazal count five fears of the weak upon the strong: of the mafgia upon the lion, of the mosquito upon the elephant, of the kilbis upon the leviathan, of the סנונית upon the eagle, and of the שממית upon the scorpion. They explained the שממית there as arania in la'az; and since Rabbeinu Hai explained the סנונית, the swallow, as the katuf in Arabic, the שממית cannot be the katuf.

סלח.sense: To forgive; he gives the word no gloss at all, only its forms, down to סַלָּח, forgiving, and סְלִיחָה, forgiveness.

more.t: The pesukim and nothing more: סָלַחְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ (Bamidbar 14:20), I have forgiven as you asked; סְֽלַֽח ־נָא לַֽעֲוֹן הָעָם הַזֶּה (Bamidbar 14:19), forgive the sin of this people; in the passive וְנִסְלַח לֽוֹ (Vayikra 4:26), and he will be forgiven; the adjective טוֹב וְסַלָּח (Tehillim 86:5), good and forgiving; and the noun כִּי־עִמְּךָ הַסְּלִיחָה (Tehillim 130:4), with You is forgiveness.

גרן.sense: The threshing floor; of the sense he says only ידוע, that it is known, and gives three pesukim.

more.t: גֹּרֶן וָיֶקֶב לֹא יִרְעֵם (Hoshea 9:2), threshing floor and winepress will not feed them; וּמָֽלְאוּ הַגֳּרָנוֹת בָּר (Yoel 2:24), the threshing floors will be full of grain; and מְדֻשָׁתִי וּבֶן־ גָּרְנִי (Yeshayahu 21:10), my threshed one and the son of my threshing floor. Of all of them he says only ידוע, it is known.

דגל.sense: The דֶּגֶל, the standard that the heads of the troops raise; and a verb comes from it, which he gives without a gloss.

more.t: דֶּגֶל מַֽחֲנֵה יְהוּדָה (Bamidbar 2:3), the standard of the camp of Yehudah, pointed בשש נקדות, with six dots. He glosses it הנס שמרימין ראשי החיילות, the standard that the heads of the troops raise.

דָּגוּל מֵרְבָבָֽה (Shir HaShirim 5:10), marked out above ten thousand; וּבְשֵֽׁם־אֱלֹהֵינוּ נִדְגֹּל (Tehillim 20:6), in the name of Hashem we will raise our banner; and אֲיֻמָּה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת (Shir HaShirim 6:4), awesome as ranks under their banners.

כתל.sense: The wall. אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ (Shir HaShirim 2:9), behind our wall, and he glosses it in two words: הוא הקיר, it is the wall.

אפה.sense: To bake. The word is always said of bread; of the other foods, he says, the word is cooking.

more.h: A thing named by what it becomes
more.t: וּמַצּוֹת אָפָה (Bereishis 19:3), he baked matzos, and וְאַף אָפִיתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו לֶחֶם (Yeshayahu 44:15), I have baked bread on its coals, are על שם סופו, after what the thing ends as, since it is not called לחם, bread, until it is baked. So too וְטַֽחֲנִי קָמַח (Yeshayahu 47:2), grind flour; וַתִּקַּח אֶת־הַבָּצֵק (Shmuel II 13:8), she took the dough and kneaded it; וּבִגְדֵי עֲרוּמִּים תַּפְשִֽׁיט (Iyov 22:6), you strip the garments of the naked; נִשְׁבְּרָה קִרְיַת־תֹּהוּ (Yeshayahu 24:10), the city of emptiness is broken; יָהֵב חָכְמְתָא לְחַכִּימִין (Daniel 2:21), He gives wisdom to the wise; יוּמַת הַמֵּת (Devarim 17:6), the dead man shall be put to death; and וְיָֽצְאוּ יְלָדֶיהָ (Shemos 21:22), her children come out, though they were not born but only fit to be children.

וַתֹּפֵהוּ מַצּֽוֹת (Shmuel I 28:24), she baked it into matzos; אֵת אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאפוּ אֵפוּ (Shemos 16:23), bake what you will bake. The baker: תַנּוּר בֹּעֵרָה מֵֽאֹפֶה (Hoshea 7:4), an oven burning from the baker, that is, מצד האופה שמבעירו, from the side of the baker who kindles it, and מִחוּץ הָֽאֹפִים (Yirmiyahu 37:21), from the street of the bakers. In the passive, לֹא תֵֽאָפֶה חָמֵץ (Vayikra 6:10), it shall not be baked leavened, and חָמֵץ תֵּֽאָפֶינָה (Vayikra 23:17). The noun is מַֽאֲפֵה תַנּוּר (Vayikra 2:4), an oven's baking.

תֻּֽפִינֵי מִנְחַת פִּתִּים (Vayikra 6:14) is another pattern, the alef exchanged for a quiescent vav with a nun added at the end. It is said in the plural because the offering was baked many bakings: scalded in boiling water, then baked in the oven, then fried again in a pan.

ציר.sense: צִיר נֶאֱמָן לְשֹֽׁלְחָיו (Mishlei 25:13), a faithful envoy to those who send him. He gives no gloss here, saying he has written the matter at the root צוּר.

שׁגר.sense: Sending forth. שְׁגַר ־אֲלָפֶיךָ (Devarim 7:13) and שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה (Shemos 13:12), which he points בשש נקודות, with six dots.

more.t: ענינם ענין שלוח, their sense is sending, as יְשַׁלְּחוּ כַצֹּאן עֲוִֽילֵיהֶם (Iyov 21:11), they send out their little ones like a flock.

Chazal say מלא שגר היונה, which he explains as שלוח היונה והליכתה, the dove's being sent out and her going. They made the word usual for sending, as שגר אחריו, he sent after him, and much else besides.

רפסד.sense: Rafts: the great logs men tie together and bring along the rivers and the sea.

more.t: רַפְסֹדוֹת עַל־יָם יָפוֹ (Divrei HaYamim II 2:15) are the דוברות named in Melachim (Melachim I 5:23), הקורות שקושרין אותן ביחד, the beams men tie together and bring along the rivers and the sea. He gives their name in the vernacular.

more.h: In the Mishnah and the Yerushalmi
more.t: The Mishnah in Berachos has היה יושב בספינה או באסדא, one who was sitting in a boat or on a raft, and the Talmud Yerushalmi there says היא אסדא היא אכסדיא היא רפסודות, the אסדא and the אכסדיא and the רפסודות are one thing.

דוג.sense: The fisherman and the fish: דַּוָּגִים is a word of description for those who hunt fish, and דָּג is the fish itself.

more.t: עָלָיו דַּוָּגִים (Yechezkel 47:10), fishermen standing over it. With a yud in place of the vav, לְדַוָּגִים (Yirmiyahu 16:16), and in the same pasuk וְדִיגוּם, and they shall fish them out.
Some grammarians say it is of the heavy verb and the yud ought to carry a dagesh. He holds it may rather be of the augmented form with the heh of the binyan dropped, the proper form being והדיגום.

דָּג גָּדוֹל (Yonah 2:1), a great fish; written with an alef in מְבִיאִים דָּאג (Nechemiah 13:16), bringing fish; דְּגֵי הַיָּם (Bamidbar 11:22), the fish of the sea; in the feminine מִמְּעֵי הַדָּגָֽה (Yonah 2:2), from the belly of the fish; and as a collective וְהַדָּגָה אֲשֶׁר־בַּיְאֹר תָּמוּת (Shemos 7:18), the fish in the river will die, דְגַת ־יְאֹרֶיךָ (Yechezkel 29:4), the fish of your rivers, and תִּבְאַשׁ דְּגָתָם מֵאֵין מַיִם (Yeshayahu 50:2), their fish stink for want of water. He says he has already written of these at the root דָּגָה.
בְּסִירוֹת דּוּגָֽה (Amos 4:2), for which he gives no gloss.

טמן.sense: To hide. All of them, he says, are ענין הסתר והעלמה, the sense of concealing and putting out of sight.

more.t: טָמַן עָצֵל יָדוֹ בַּצַּלָּחַת (Mishlei 19:24), the sluggard buries his hand in the dish; טָמְנוּ פַח לִֽי (Tehillim 142:4), they hid a trap for me; וּטְמַנְתָּם בַּמֶּלֶט (Yirmiyahu 43:9), hide them in the mortar; וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַמִּצְרִי וַֽיִּטְמְנֵהוּ בַּחֽוֹל (Shemos 2:12), he struck the Mitzri and hid him in the sand; וַיִּטְמֹן אֹתָם יַֽעֲקֹב תַּחַת הָֽאֵלָה (Bereishis 35:4), Yaakov hid them under the terebinth; and לִטְמוֹן בְּחֻבִּי עֲוֹֽנִי (Iyov 31:33), to hide my sin in my bosom.
In the passive, וְהִטָּמֵן בֶּֽעָפָר (Yeshayahu 2:10), hide yourself in the dust; and in another form, וַיֵּֽלְכוּ וַיַּטְמִנוּ (Melachim II 7:8), they went and hid it away.

נָתַן לָכֶם מַטְמוֹן (Bereishis 43:23), He has given you a hidden store; כִּֽי־יֶשׁ־לָנוּ מַטְמֹנִים בַּשָּׂדֶה (Yirmiyahu 41:8), we have stores hidden in the field; and with a shuruk, וּמַטְמֻנֵי מִסְתָּרִים (Yeshayahu 45:3), hoards in secret places. On פְּנֵיהֶם חֲבֹשׁ בַּטָּמֽוּן (Iyov 40:13) he says the word means למקום שיטמינם בו, the place where He hides them.

גנז.sense: Treasuries. He glosses them כמו אוצרות, like storehouses: a place, or vessels, into which gold and silver and precious garments are put.

more.t: Two pesukim and a line: אֶל־ גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (Esther 3:9), to the king's treasuries, and וּבְגִנְזֵי בְּרֹמִים (Yechezkel 27:24).

שׁמשׁ.sense: The sun; and from it שִׁמְשֹׁתַיִךְ, the windows the sun comes in by.

more.t: שֶׁמֶשׁ יָרֵחַ עָמַד זְבֻלָה (Chavakuk 3:11), pointed בשש נקודות, with six dots, and meaning שמש וירח, the sun and the moon.

יוֹמָם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לֹֽא־יַכֶּכָּה (Tehillim 121:6), by day the sun will not strike you; הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יָצָא עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 19:23), the sun had come out over the earth; וְזָרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ (Koheles 1:5), the sun rises; לֹֽא־יָבוֹא עוֹד שִׁמְשֵׁךְ (Yeshayahu 60:20), your sun will set no more; שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה (Malachi 3:20), a sun of righteousness; and לְעֵינֵי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ הַזֹּֽאת (Shmuel II 12:11), before this sun.
וְשַׂמְתִּי כַּֽדְכֹד שִׁמְשֹׁתַיִךְ (Yeshayahu 54:12), which he glosses החלונות שהשמש נכנס בהם, the windows the sun enters by.

סהר.sense: The moon: the Targum of יָרֵחַ is סִיהֲרָא. From it the round ornaments of the women are named, and the round prison.

more.t: שָׁרְרֵךְ אַגַּן הַסַּהַר (Shir HaShirim 7:3), and the Targum of יָרֵחַ (Tehillim 8:4) is סִיהֲרָא.

For this reason מראות הנשים, the women's mirrors, are called שהרונים, as וְהַשְּׁבִיסִים וְהַשַּֽׂהֲרֹנִֽים (Yeshayahu 3:18), because they are like the סהר. That word, he notes, is written with a sin.
בֵּית הַסֹּהַר (Bereishis 39:20) is the name of the prison, שהוא עגול בדמות הסהר, because it is round in the likeness of the moon.

מנח.sense: The מִנְחָה. The entry is on whether its mem belongs to the root, and on the evening offering and the hour of prayer named from it.

more.h: Whether the mem is of the root
more.t: On וַיָּכִינוּ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָה (Bereishis 43:25) and אַל־תֵּפֶן אֶל־ מִנְחָתָם (Bamidbar 16:15): some say the mem is of the root. It may rather be added and the root נָחָה, and that is the closer to the sense, since מנחה is of the sense of נחה, a thing set down, as אֲרוּחָה is named from אָרַח. But the truth cannot be settled, because the plural is not found in Scripture.

Since they read מנחות in the Mishnah with a sheva under the mem, and so it is read in every mouth, מְנָחוֹת, the mem looks to be of the root: as from גִּבְעָה you say גְּבָעוֹת, so from מִנְחָה you say מְנָחוֹת. Were the mem added, it should have carried a chirik, as מִצְוָה gives מִצְוֹת and מַחְתָּה gives מַחְתּוֹת.

The evening olah is called מנחה: הַקְטֵר אֶת־עֹֽלַת־הַבֹּקֶר וְאֶת־ מִנְחַת הָעֶרֶב (Melachim II 16:15), and מַֽשְׂאַת כַּפַּי מִנְחַת ־עָֽרֶב (Tehillim 141:2), the lifting of my hands as an evening offering. וַיְהִי בַּֽעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה וַיִּגַּשׁ אֵֽלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא (Melachim I 18:36) means at the hour the מנחה went up. The morning olah too is called מנחה, at the hour they bring the morning offering.

more.h: The prayer named from the hour
more.t: The prayer of מנחה is so called because it falls at the hour the evening מנחה goes up, והוא עת נטות השמש, the time the sun turns down. So וַֽאֲנִי ישֵׁב מְשׁוֹמֵם עַד לְמִנְחַת הָעָֽרֶב (Ezra 9:4), I sat appalled until the evening מנחה, and וּבְמִנְחַת הָעֶרֶב קַמְתִּי מִתַּֽעֲנִיתִי (Ezra 9:5), at the evening מנחה I rose from my fast.

נתן.sense: To give. He sets out the forms and at the end says only ענינם ידוע, their sense is known.

more.t: On וְאֹיְבַי תַּתָּה לִּי עֹרֶף (Shmuel II 22:41), You gave me the back of my enemies, he notes בחסרון הקצוות, the ends of the word missing, not as the past tense usually runs. וַאֲנַחְנוּ נִתַּן ־לָךְ (Shoftim 16:5), and we will give you, carries a patach, לגזרת אֶפְעַל, for the אפעל pattern. And לְתִתֵּן שָׁם אֶת־אֲרוֹן בְּרִית (Melachim I 6:19), to set the ark of the covenant there, he calls an infinitive with a nun added at the end.

וַיִּתֶּן ־יָד (Bereishis 38:28), he put out a hand; תְּנָה אֶת־יָדֶךָ (Melachim II 10:15), give your hand; נָתְנוּ יָד תַּחַת שְׁלֹמֹה (Divrei HaYamim I 29:24), they gave the hand under Shlomo; and מִצְרַיִם נָתַנּוּ יָד (Eichah 5:6), Mitzrayim gave the hand. He sets them in a row and glosses none of them.

נִתְּנָה רֹאשׁ (Bamidbar 14:4), let us set a head; וְנָתוֹן אֹתוֹ עַל כָּל־אֶרֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (Bereishis 41:43), setting him over all the land of Mitzrayim; תְּנוּ אֶת־אֲרֽוֹן־הַקֹּדֶשׁ בַּבַּיִת (Divrei HaYamim II 35:3), put the holy ark in the house; נְתֻנִים נְתֻנִים הֵמָּה לִי (Bamidbar 8:16), given, given they are to Me; and שְֽׂאוּ־זִמְרָה וּתְנוּ ־תֹף (Tehillim 81:3), raise a song and sound the drum.

כְּבוֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן נִתַּן ־לָהּ (Yeshayahu 35:2), the glory of Levanon was given her; וְהִוא לֹֽא־ נִתְּנָה לוֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה (Bereishis 38:14), she was not given him to wife; תֶּבֶן אֵין נִתָּן לַֽעֲבָדֶיךָ (Shemos 5:16), no straw is given your servants; and הִנָּתֹן תִּנָּתֵן הָעִיר הַזֹּאת (Yirmiyahu 38:3), this city will surely be given. Where the doer is not named, וְכִי יֻֽתַּן ־מַיִם עַל־זֶרַע (Vayikra 11:38), if water be put on seed.

וּמִן־ הַנְּתִינִים שֶׁנָּתַן דָּוִיד וְהַשָּׂרִים לַֽעֲבֹדַת הַֽלְוִיִּם (Ezra 8:20), of the Nesinim whom David and the officers gave for the service of the Leviim. The nouns are מֹהַר וּמַתָּן (Bereishis 34:12), bride price and gift; תְּרוּמַת מַתָּנָם (Bamidbar 18:11); עֲבֹדַת מַתָּנָה (Bamidbar 18:7); אִישׁ כְּמַתְּנַת יָדוֹ (Devarim 16:17), each man according to the gift of his hand; and in another pattern וְאֶתְּנָה לְךָ מַתָּֽת (Melachim I 13:7), and I will give you a gift.

תור.sense: To search out and explore; also the turtledove, a turn or a time, and the sense of תכונה, the measure or condition of a thing.

more.t: תַּרְתִּי בְלִבִּי (Koheles 2:3), I searched in my heart; אֲשֶׁר תָּרוּ אֹתָהּ (Bamidbar 13:32), the land they spied out; וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַֽחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם (Bamidbar 15:39), do not go searching after your heart. וַיָּתִירוּ בֵֽית־יוֹסֵף (Shoftim 1:23) is חקירה וחפוש, examining and searching, and from the same is יְתוּר הָרִים מִרְעֵהוּ (Iyov 39:8), he searches the mountains for his pasture, a noun of the pattern of יְקוּם and יְבוּל.

לְבַד מֵֽאַנְשֵׁי הַתָּרִים וְהַסֹּֽחֲרִים (Divrei HaYamim II 9:14): the התרים are the lesser traders, few in goods and dealings, who search hard over what they buy and sell because their business is small, while the סוחרים are the great merchants.
By the Targum's reading, דֶּרֶךְ הָֽאֲתָרִים (Bamidbar 21:1) belongs to this root, the alef being added.

וְתֹר וְגוֹזָֽל (Bereishis 15:9), a turtledove and a young pigeon; וְהִקְרִיב מִן־ הַתֹּרִים (Vayikra 1:14); and שְׁתֵּי תֹרִים (Vayikra 5:7), two turtledoves, of which he says ידוע, it is known. The pasuk says הָאֶחָד in the masculine and שְׁתֵּי in the feminine to teach that male and female are alike fit. From this, אַל־תִּתֵּן לְחַיַּת נֶפֶשׁ תּוֹרֶךָ (Tehillim 74:19), where Knesses Yisrael is likened to a turtledove, as she is likened also to a dove.

more.h: A time, and a man's measure
more.t: תֹּר נַֽעֲרָה וְנַֽעֲרָה (Esther 2:12) is ענינו זמן, a time. וּרְאִיתַנִי כְּתוֹר הָֽאָדָם הַמַּֽעֲלָה (Divrei HaYamim I 17:17) is כתכונת האדם, after the measure of a man: this greatness You have spoken of me is the measure of a great man, but what am I and what is my house, and so he says הַמַּעֲלָה, that You saw me in the measure of a great man though I am small and lowly. So too וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָֽאָדָם (Shmuel II 7:19).

more.h: The Torah, and the rows of pearls
more.t: It may be that וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה (Devarim 4:44) is of this root, and the Torah of Hashem that is perfect (Tehillim 19:8), all of them one in this sense, since they mean תכונה, a fixed measure, as he explained at the root יָרָה. Near to it is נָאווּ לְחָיַיִךְ בַּתֹּרִים (Shir HaShirim 1:10), the pearls joined and set in order.

למד.sense: To learn, and in the doubled form to teach; ענינם הלמוד וההרגל, their sense is learning and habit.

more.t: בַּל־ לָמַד צֶדֶק (Yeshayahu 26:10), he has not learned righteousness, which he marks מלרע, stressed on the last syllable; יִשְׁמְעוּ וְלָמְדוּ (Devarim 31:13), they will hear and learn; לְמַעַן יִלְמַד לְיִרְאָה (Devarim 17:19); וַיִּלְמַד לִטְרָף־טֶרֶף (Yechezkel 19:3), he learned to tear prey; and אִם־ לָמֹד יִלְמְדוּ אֶת־דַּֽרְכֵי עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 12:16), if they will indeed learn the ways of My people.

לִמַּד ־דַּעַת (Koheles 12:9), he taught knowledge; רְאֵה לִמַּדְתִּי אֶתְכֶם (Devarim 4:5), see, I have taught you; אֲשֶׁר אָֽנֹכִי מְלַמֵּד אֶתְכֶם (Devarim 4:1), which I teach you; עֶגְלָה מְלֻמָּדָה (Hoshea 10:11), a trained heifer; מְלֻמְּדֵי מִלְחָמָה (Shir HaShirim 3:8), trained in war; and where the doer is not named, כְּעֵגֶל לֹא לֻמָּד (Yirmiyahu 31:17), like a calf untrained.

וּלְמוּדֵי מִלְחָמָה, those trained for war; פֶּרֶה לִמֻּד מִדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 2:24), a wild donkey used to the wilderness; לְשׁוֹן לִמּוּדִים (Yeshayahu 50:4), the tongue of the taught; לִמֻּדֵי הָרֵֽעַ (Yirmiyahu 13:23), trained to do evil; and Yeshayahu 54:13, all your children taught of Hashem. In another pattern, כַּקָּטֹן כַּגָּדוֹל מֵבִין עִם־ תַּלְמִֽיד (Divrei HaYamim I 25:8), the small as the great, the one who understands with the learner.

אַשּׁוּר כִּלֽמַד רֹֽכַלְתֵּֽךְ (Yechezkel 27:23) is of the pattern of כָּבֵד, and in the construct לְמַד, as כְבַד ־פֶּה (Shemos 4:10). His father writes that the men of Ashur were as those accustomed to come to you always in trade, and he says he will write further at the root רָכַל.

From this the staff with the needle fixed in its head, the one called a דָּֽרְבָן, is named מלמד: בְּמַלְמַד הַבָּקָר (Shoftim 3:31), the goad of the oxen, לפי שמלמד ומורה הבקר לחרישה, because it teaches and directs the oxen to plough.
